title: Solved my issue
text_original:
I wasn't very happy to need this part in the first place. For an LG refrigerator that was about $2500, I would have expected it to last more than 3 years. However, I'd rather put in a $100 part than buy a whole new one.

What is this board for? It is the smaller of the 2 boards inside, and acts as the power supply to the compressor.
Symptoms: Refrigerator may be blowing air, but isn't cooling.
Touch the compressor (the large black "ball" inside the rear at the bottom, behind the large metal panel). If it is room temp or just slightly warmer (not hot), and the small condenser fan on the right is moving (which indicates the other board and thermostat are fine), then this smaller board (behind a small metal panel a bit higher up on the back should get you up and running again.
You can get these cheaper elsewhere such as encompass or other appliance parts sites, but amazon typically has quick prime shipping, so it was worth the extra cost to get the fridge back in working order quickly.

title: Does what I need it to.
text_original:
I am disabled and live on the second floor of an apartment building. the community laundry is on the first floor and often out-of-order. Getting up and down the stairs is not always easy for me and paying for washers and dryers that are out of order are not exactly what I want to be doing.

This washer has saved me from having to make multiple trips up and down the stairs. The fill hose is just plastic, There is no coupler or adaptor on it, but in reality I don't feel that this hose is needed. I fill the washer with a mop bucked. it takes about 3 8quart buckets to fill the washer completely full, give or take how much you are washing and how much water you need to cover the clothing. I've washed jeans, and even full sized bed sheets. *no - your blankets wont fit in this and certainly not the spin tub. and you do have to be careful not to add to heavy an item into it because the wash agitator can only take so much. This is perfect for someone that is single and just wants to get their day to day clothing clean without running to the laundery Mat. It's light enough that you can pick it up and store it away in a small closet when not in use.
a lot of people show videos where they put the washer in the bath tub. I guess they were afraid it would leak. I would warn against doing this unless you have something to set it on top of to keep it from getting wet underneath because your motors for both the wash tub and the spin tub are on the bottom of the washer. In fact this is the only real problem with this product is needing something to set it on top of. I put mine on top of two single step rubber maid step stools. (one isn't wide enough) and just keep it near the kitchen sink where I can fill a mop bucket to fill it and use the drain hose to drain it into the mop bucket when I'm done, or in between wash and rinse cycels. The gravity draining makes it easy to just put the hose up and turn off drain to empty the bucket. very easy, just an extra step or two.

I seen someone asked where the product was made. I looked when I seen that asked but there is nothing on the product or it's documentation telling you where it was made. sorry. Maybe the seller can tell you.

update May 2021 This product did not last a year. I purchased it late May and received it in June of 2020. While it was working it did a great job, exactly what I needed it to do. But early May 2020 the washer side stopped working. it started with the timer. first it started to get stuck then it just wouldn't tick at all like an old cooking timer when they have seen years of use. I thought maybe I just need to get the timer replaced in it. I continued to use the spinner side but a couple of weeks after the washer side stopped working then the spinner gave out. one day it worked the next day it simply would not even turn on to spin. so I don't know if this helps anyone else but I'm not the first one to notice this same situation so apparently it's repeatable by others in this product. just be aware it's not built to last. It was great until it quit working.

title: No problems!  Worth the savings.
text_original:
I purchased these filters to replace the GE Model MWF filter which is much more expensive. Granted that the GE filter is NSF Standards 42 & 53, and these filters are only NSF Standard 42. Standard 53 is nice to have, but our water supply is safe, and I use the filter for purposes of improving taste.

No problems replacing filter, and NO LEAKS as has been described by some. You must make sure that the O-ring is in place. I didn't have to turn off water to refrigerator since it has automatic shut-off when filter is removed. I think these are worth the $10/filter savings vs. the GE.

I gave it a 4 STAR rating since it does not meet NSF Standard 53.

NSF/ANSI Standard 42: Drinking Water Treatment Units - Aesthetic Effects
Overview: This standard covers point-of-use (POU) and point-of-entry (POE) systems designed to reduce specific aesthetic or non-health-related contaminants (chlorine, taste and odor, and particulates) that may be present in public or private drinking water.

NSF/ANSI Standard 53: Drinking Water Treatment Units - Health Effects
Overview: Standard 53 addresses point-of-use (POU) and point-of-entry (POE) systems designed to reduce specific health-related contaminants, such as Cryptosporidium, Giardia, lead, volatile organic chemicals (VOCs), MTBE (methyl tertiary-butyl ether), that may be present in public or private drinking water.

title: AVOID! Component failure / defrosting required or fridge stops cooling
text_original:
It is my view that Samsung is negligent having failed to advertise this fridge as requiring defrosting, and selling these fridges with full knowledge they are not performing as advertised - and in fact fail to perform the purpose they are intended for, for a period of time that is well within reasonable expectations. I bought this fridge in Sept. 2014 and it needs defrosting periodically. The cabinet housing the fans builds up with ice to the point the fan stops and the fridge ceases to cool effectively.

The internet is filled with people having the precise same problem as I am, and videos on how to remove the ice build up (hairdryer works) so I have to believe this is not a singular problem I am having but a characteristic of their fridges. There is a class action in the USA.

Samsung does not include info on how to defrost in their manual nor do they offer any workaround, or information such as "where will the water come from as it defrosts". Yet the call centre folks don't even need to consult a manual to tell you how to defrost it ... you have to put it in something called "shop mode" and wait 24 hours.

They offer this product with a 10 year warranty, which I took as a company willing to stand behind their product, yet this commonly experienced design problem is not covered. I believe as a consumer I need protection from this company's shoddy design and lack of responsibility for their malfunctioning product. And so it seems does anyone buying a Samsung fridge. The model is the RF23HCEDBSR.

title: Great Kegerator!
text_original:
I bought this kegerator for my boyfriend for Christmas and he absolutely loves it.

Bought it with Prime and it came in 2 days. Packaging was fine. No dents. One of the removable shelves was bent but was not a concern because we plan on using 1/2 barrel kegs mostly so both shelves would need to be removed anyway.

Did not give it 5 stars because of the directions! They are not clear! I would recommend watching as many YouTube videos you can about the assembly. Some parts are not as described as others have reviewed on here like the color of the CO2 tubing. Had an issue when we tapped the first keg, had the wrong washer for the beer line to coupler connection. Also, Do not remove the duck bill from the CO2 line input! After we figured those out we had no issues. No problems with exchanging the CO2 tank at a local welding supply shop.

Overall, the kegerator has been great! We are on our 2nd 1/2 barrel keg of Miller Lite. Friends enjoy coming over to use it. Biggest concern when purchasing was if it would fit MillerCoors 1/2 barrel kegs. Ask your distributor if their MillerCoors kegs are standard 1/2 barrel and not the oversized rubberized ones. We have not had an issue yet. Would highly recommend this product for a first time kegerator users!

title: Easy to install, but annoying to the ears!
text_original: While this motor is easy to install, it's noisier than the 15 year-old motor I replaced. By contrast, I have purchased genuine Nutone OEM motors over the years & the fan was significantly quieter after motor replacement. Motors with a sleeve bearing (instead of a ball bearing assembly) at each end of the rotor & a rotor that may not be perfectly balanced contribute to a louder noise level in operation. Exhaust fans made in recent years have improved designs & reduced noise levels. If you're bothered by the constant, low-pitch rumbling of a noisy replacement motor, it's probably time to replace the whole fan unit - even if it does involve more work. Your ears will appreciate it.

title: POOR QC!  One of the valves leaks (drips) where its solenoid attaches to blue plastic body
text_original:
It was not a good idea for me to buy this cheap version of this part; lesson learned! This is a key part of your washing machine, and if cheaply made can cause a flood in your home. Installation was straightforward, but upon turning on the hot and cold water supply lines, one of the valves immediately started dripping where its valve solenoid meets the blue plastic valve body. Must have been poorly sealed at the factory. Luckily, I noticed the drip before I walked away!

Needless to say, I'm going to seek a refund and try to find a better-made one -- Hopefully they don't all come from the same foreign factory (from the product photos, they sure look like they do).

If you're going to take a chance on this brand, I recommend that you test both of its valves for leaks by connecting them (one at a time) to a water supply hose, before you bother installing it into your washer. You can just turn off your washer's water supply lines, connect the cold water supply line to the valve you're testing, hold the valve assembly over the tub of your washer to catch any drips, then turn on the supply line and check for leaks. You do not need to connect the electrical lines, because the solenoid valves are, by design, automatically closed when power is NOT applied.

No instructions for the not so inclined...but with forethought and patience..... 1. clean the surface very well with alcohol and klean dry cotton (twice), 2. then wipe the residue from alcohol off with a clean dry cotton cloth. 3. Use tweezers to pull stickers at the point of fold and apply slowly / carefully (it will stick immediately with the help of static stiction), NOTE A. think it through as to where the sticker will go exactly. B. Use the dot sticker as a datum line and apply each of the dots evenly across the panel, C. apply the flame icon under each dot.
It is also wise to think thru the layout of each sticker icon of each burner location. Yes I wasn't paying attention and applied one incorrectly. Not to worry, an extra couple decals are on the sheet.

title: Save yourself some emotional angst and do NOT buy this dryer
text_original:
Glad to know I'm not the only one with issues with this dryer. Thirty minutes after it was hooked up (and the delivery guys were back on their way), it started making a sound like the bearing in the motor had gone bad. I timed it, and the "click, click, click" was 60 times per minute. Fortunately, the merchant offered an exchange.

Then Problem #2 began, and it's actually a much bigger problem.

Whomever designed this overpriced appliance did something wanky to the baffles in the drum, because I didn't have this problem with my old (Samsung) dryer. I can not dry any bedding in this new dryer (purchased 8.2015) because it tangles up everything into such a tight ball that my sheets are ruined. My new policy is to stand at the dryer and open the door every 1-2 minutes, remove all the sheets, shake them out and re-insert. It doesn't take a full minute for everything to get wrapped up in a super tight wad. I have come here to look into buying a traditional clothes line because this dryer is such a piece of junk.

I've tried drying the sheets with dryer balls, with large beach towels, with small towels and even with towels knotted up. Last week, I washed and dried my tennis shoes with the sheets and even that didn't stop the sheets from getting twisted up and tied up in knots.

I don't have the money to buy another $800 dryer, so I've written a letter to Samsung corporate. We'll see how that works out.

title: Weak Center Burner & thin griddle
text_original:
I've had this dual oven for a while now and all things considered, it is a very good looking unit and the performance outside of the center burner is very good.

The dual oven feature is great and helps when cooking multiple items. I've used the convection on the lower oven a few times now and has worked well with both desserts as well as dinner items like casseroles and lasagnas. The upper smaller oven heats up quickly and although the grate doesnt slide as well as it should, the oven works quite well.

The main beef I have with this unit is the low BTU output (8k) of the center burner. When speaking with multiple associates about this, they say it isn't supposed to be your main cooking option and that's why the output isnt great. I kind of took this with a grain of salt but after using the center burner and griddle combo for a little bit of time now, I have unfortunately concluded that its just not enough heat emitting from it. I was trying to be patient the first few times and didnt write this review until I gave it a fair shake but after using it this weekend 2 more times, I sadly have to say that it just doesn't have the punch to really cook something sufficiently. I'm not looking for a super high sear or a charring effect but when it takes 2+ minutes to finally have the bubbles of a pancake surface, I think that is just a little too long. Also since this griddle is a little thin compared to the other brands (GE and KitchenAid were much thicker and heavier while Samsung was roughly the same density), there seemed to be a couple more hot spots (near the back half) than I would have expected.

I don't want to knock this oven entirely since most of the competitors are between 8k-10k BTU's as well so this might just be the industry standard. Again I would have just wished that the heat output be just a little higher in order to give this center burner a little more versatility than what it currently is.

Outside of this, the oven looks great and performs quite well.

title: Decent despite some manufacturing and packaging foibles
text_original:
I hate messing with egg cartons, so decided to give this storage organizer a try. The design overall is well thought out, with the two trays stacking together and slightly pitched so the remaining eggs in each row roll to the front as you take one out. The handles are hollow and easy to grab. It has a month and day manual timer on the top to keep track of the expiration date; to be honest, I go through eggs so quickly that I will likely never use that feature, but it's nice that they included it.

A couple things I did notice that kept this from being scored higher. One, there were no instructions in the box. It's easy enough to figure out how to put in the handle inserts and the track on the bottom tray by looking at the pictures on here, but I still think any product that requires assembly should have instructions provided, even if it's one sheet. Two, the top lid was slightly warped, so it took a little effort to get it to snap in properly.

Overall, it's useful and probably worth it if you go through tons of eggs like me, and also like me, you hate screwing around with paper (or even worse) plastic egg cartons.

title: HAZARDOUS FOR HUMAN SKIN WHEN DRY
text_original:
This review is on the chemical itself, not the seller on Amazon. This chemical compound looks like salt. It is used in just about every diaper brand.

As an absorbing product, it does, but not as it claims. My grandson was using Luvs and we used between 8-12 diapers a day. He is 6 months old. That equates to at minimum 1 an hour or less. They leak. They dont keep the urine off the skin. That is what causes diaper rash.

For my grandson, there was a different issue. He had what we thought was a friction irritation from the outer elastic area. We called to make sure if they used latex. Both I and his Mommy are allergic so it doesnt hurt to be on the safe side. They said no.

My daughter in law took an unused diaper and cut into the diaper to double check. Cotton, maybe rayon, & the salt looking stuff. In a few seconds of her looking for latex, she began getting itchy hives all over. PowPow (Grandpa) came and got me. Im a disabled medic. Bad spine injury a couple years ago.

He told me about it and slapped some wet crystal like goop on my arm. Nothing. Then he put salt on my other arm. Sure enough, red itchy hives in seconds. Guess what else... PowPow started itching too.

So he looked up the salt and I called Luvs (Pampers Sister Co aka Proctor & Gamble, my favorite company of household necessities). They dont call it sodium polyacrylate. Its hbm or something, but its the same. They are sending a care package to retrieve 2 diapers for testing and pictures of our rashes. They are sending coupons, but um, hello!!! Not to mention we took the rest of the diapers back to Walmart for a full refund, went back to the diaper aisle and called White Cloud (not Walmarts brand surprisingly) & found out the ingredientsare simple & non chemical & hypoallergenic & less in cost.

I put more salt on my forearm where it would stay dry and bandaged it with a breathable cloth bandaid for testing. When I woke up, there was red hives outside of the bandage.

So dry, this stuff is a severe skin irritant or burning chemical. It is plentiful in most baby diapers. It is in MOST BABY DIAPERS. I cannot stress that enough. No matter how much Desitin or A & D or corn starch you use, the diaper rash will expand. No matter if you check every 5 minutes and change your baby every time they potty right away. This chemical is on their butts 23.5 hours a day 365 days times two or three. That is too much suffering. Sodium polyacrylate is a great absorption product for everything that does not touch people, especially babies.

title: Scratches are GONE. A Spectacular Result. Meets All Expectations.
text_original:
Read the instructions and explicitly follow them to remove blemishes and scratches. Don't rush, take your time, and you will be very happy with the result. Scratches and blemishes will be gone. Of course, this won't remove a dent, but at least it won't be a dent with a scratch.

I needed to use the finger thick piece of sand paper, due to having deep scratches, followed by the foam backed burgundy pad with the special lubricant that is supplied. I then finished it off with the gray pad. After using the course paper, you need to blend it all in using the pads. Take your time and go with the grain. GO WITH THE GRAIN.

The picture shows a perfect result. Right below that window in the center of the microwave were three perfectly vertical 1/4" long scratches. No more scratches. Wow, this is a wonderful product that meet all expectations.

title: Great ice maker, but high maintenance
text_original:
Takes about 15 minutes to start getting ice, about 30 minutes to fill a glass, and the nugget/pebble/sonic ice cubes are as good as you'll get anywhere. It'll run for hours reliably, hasn't yet leaked, and is fairly easy to move. Your house guests will be sold on purchasing their own immediately.

The ice maker is good enough to make refrigerator ice makers unnecessary in the future. You'd rather have one of these alongside the fridge than spend $200-$400 to take up space inside the fridge. If only the Opal could connect to the fridge's PEX water line as well. It's a minor annoyance that pales in comparison to the real downsides.

The real downsides:

After a month or two, it'll start making weird, whiny, almost injured sounds for the first hour after it's turned on. It'll make you think the machine is broken or in process of breaking. Once you're relieved of that fear, you'll just be left annoyed as opposed to being worried. This will also cause your house guests to reconsider getting their own machine.

Cleaning it takes a long time. FirstBuild recommends 3 different cleaners (vinegar, bleach, and their proprietary cleaner), but isn't clear why you would use one over the other. The cleaning process takes 3 cleaning cycles of vinegar or the cleaning solution (1 cycle of bleach+water), followed by 3 cycles of fresh water to fully clean the machine. You must also let the machine sit for an hour before you begin the cleaning process. This process becomes rather annoying, and means you won't be making ice that day, so plan accordingly and fill an ice bucket before you begin cleaning it.

title: Worked better than my Kenmore, for 10 days
text_original:
Update: Same day I left my review, I decided to lift the machine, drain any residual water in tube, and rotate the impeller by hand, and rotate the spin tub by hand too. Suddenly it started working again! Maybe it just needed to cool off, or there was lint caught, i don't know. But it's working. But please read below, anyway.

Original review: I've had my machine less than 2 weeks, maybe 10 days. My Kenmore has been in disrepair for over a year and a half, so I got this to help me. First of all, I'll clarify. I bought mine directly from Zeny, as the delivery dates offered here at that time, were out of the date range I needed. But I'm still submitting a review for the product only, here. I love this machine! It was working great until today. We came home from a hot sweaty day trip and I was excited to get washing. I truly enjoy this machine. I had prefilled the tub with one standard bath towel, a lightweight sarong, a mask, a pair of leggings, and a washcloth, maybe 1 or 2 small things more. Added a tiny amount of soap and started it up for 6 minute wash. I noticed it was sluggish, but was set for the more powerful of the two settings. I realized that maybe I just had a tad too much in there perhaps. And the bin was at least 2/3 to 3/4 full with water too. It suddenly stopped working. I removed the towel hoping the lighter load would engage, and it would work. Nope.
I tried the spinner and that dial too, moved with ease. Normally,
There is a ticking noise the dial makes when you turn it clockwise. The timer for spin was suddenly too easy to turn (no ticking), and the spin cycle stopped working too. I'm crushed. I was just bragging about this machine. I referred to the manual, and it mentioned belts. I can see a black belt thru the plastic bottom. It seemed fine, but I'm not a technician. But with both sides of the machine, I could hear the motor trying to engage, but neither tub would work. So it's Saturday evening. I tried live chat, I've tried the phone number. I'll try Monday. It's only 10 days old. Something isn't right.

I also tried to wash 2 bath towels yesterday and the cycle was sluggish. I had done maybe 3 or 4 consecutive mini loads, with 5 minutes or less wash time. I only spin for 1 minute. Maybe a belt is loose.

So if any reviewers had a similar problem or some advice, please feel free to email me at cgee642@gmail.com. I'd be grateful. I believe in this machine, but you need to be kind to it.

Maybe one of you can help me before Monday. I thought maybe I overheated the engineand it needs to cool. I'm truly sad. It's a fun machine. I use it in the bathtub, with the power cord not near any wetness or spray. I used the shower hose to fill the washer and spray the spin tub to assist rinsing.

title: Works well for me
text_original:
Purchased this at Home Depot about 2 years ago because I loved how it looked. I also liked the extra large capacity.

I use this machine to run 2-3 loads every week. Sometimes 2 load and sometimes 3, depending on my load. I haven't had any mold or odor problems and I haven't noticed any lack of water. If anything, I think it puts in more water than it should because the machine rotates the dry load to sense how big it is. Problem is that rotating the dry load makes the load higher in certain areas, which is why I think I get more water than needed.

As for how well the machine cleans, I don't have any complaints. My clothes come out clean.

There are 3 issues though:
(1) there is always water in the bleach reservoir, which is annoying. After reading a review, I think I know how to clean it out now.
(2) the agitating motion really twists your clothes toghether. It's a struggle getting the clothes out of the dryer because they are all tangled together. This means it's really heavy to take it out as one huge clump. Or, you have to really work at untangling items. I'm good about putting my stuff into washer bags so I haven't had any issues with knit items stretching out.
(3) Lint and other gunk collect along the top rim. I'm not sure how to clean that out because the tub clean cycle definitely doesn't do it.

I could tell one of my drum wheels needed to be replaced, as I could here it was off knocking when the drum turned. I figured I'd replace both of the front ones at once since I was already in there. So I swapped out both wheels and spun the drum by hand. I could still hear the knocking. I tore the dryer apart, puked the drum out, checked both of the rear wheels and they worked fine. I was so frustrated that I couldn't find the source of the knocking. I reached down to grab the front bezel where the new wheels were mounted, and noticed one of the new ones I had installed wasn't perfectly round, but instead had a but of a warp in on side. I pulled this one off and replaced it with one of the old ones, and tada! The knocking was gone!

It was a great price, even just for one, considering it was delivered for free the next day, but I wish I had been able to replace both as I had expected.

title: 000 for a good induction cooktop
text_original:
I bought the Rosewell about six months ago because I had been thinking about replacing my old gas stove with an induction cooktop and electric oven. I wanted a trial before spending more than $1,000 for a good induction cooktop. The Rosewill has shown me that induction can provide some speed and safety, but it has also shown me that I am unlikely to buy another Rosewill model.
It has a difference in its "five speeds" and all, including the "warm milk" setting, bring water to a boil. Unfortunately, things like spaghetti sauce and others that I would like to simmer, boil instead.
I am not sure about the heat differences between "Stir-fry" and "Fry" either and have concluded the five settings do not offer much.
If you depend on the numerical temperature settings you will need to adjust and unless water boils at 150 degrees they are not accurate. I have determined that temperature settings actually range from "boiling hot" to "as hot as the Rosewill can get," whatever that is.
The pot has a nice lid, but is actually more like a stainless steel tin can than something like a decent stainless steel Dutch oven.
There is a nice smooth surface on the device with a circle in the center that shows just where to put that tin can pot and that helps. The area that actually produces the heat is considerably smaller than the total space within that circle. It is more like the size of the flame from one of the larger burners on my gas range.
All things considered, I would not rate it at more than 3 stars except that prices seem to usually be in the $60 - $80 range and with that price it seems like a decent deal and vastly cheaper than something like a Kenmore or Bosch. It's just the quite simple, "you get what you pay for" truth and that price makes it seem reasonable to rate it at 4 stars.
Its good aspects have helped me to decide that I will buy one of those that cost $2,000 or more, if I win the lottery. Not sure about any others.

title: It's OK. Better than using a spoon.
text_original:
I was excited to try this out, thinking it would be a huge improvement over pouring coffee out of a can, or using a spoon. Well, it was better alright, but not amazing. If you're half asleep, trying to make coffee, you'll probably spill some.

You have to pay attention to what you're doing. You have to keep the halves separate while you use the scoop to dig into the coffee, careful not to get too much, or you'll make a mess. You might even overfill the K-cup substitute, or whatever receptacle you are using to hold the coffee for brewing. Once the scoop is loaded with coffee, you carefully flip the top over, holding the halves together, and point the hole in the top half at the coffee receptacle to dump it in. After that, you simply bang the whole thing against the trash can, to empty out the excess. Which you will have if you didn't get just the right amount into the scoop in the first place. Even if you did get just the right amount, some of the coffee seems determined to stay behind, unless you really bang it against the side of the trash can, letting the halves fall apart while you do so.

So it works OK. Far better than using a spoon, or trying to dump the coffee out of a can. But only slightly better than simply tapping a paper coffee bag to place coffee grounds directly into the brewing receptacle. Your mileage may vary.

title: Really a nice little washer/spinner
text_original:
So Happy to have this. Wonderful little machine. One side washes with an agitator that is powerful. It really moves the clothes around. The spinner rotates at an incredible speed and the clothes are almost dry when pulled out of there, that's how well it spins the water out. I hang the clothes in the bathroom and some are dry in a few hours, others over night. Love it.
The machine does comes with a long thin tube that attaches to the washer and the other end can be attached to your kitchen or bathroom sink and you can fill the washer up with water that way, provided you remove the aerator on the sink and screw on a different aerator which that tubing will fit on. (The opening on the tubing is really small.) I am not going to go to the trouble of buying an aerator, so I fill up my washer using my shower head. Easy Peasy...The instructions do not tell you how far to fill up the washer tub with water. I fill mine up where the water reaches the bottom of the machines attached lint catcher, so just maybe half full. Regarding the spinner. After I spin the clothes, I take my shower head and fill the spinner side with some water and re-spin those clothes to make sure all detergent is washed out.
When I use the washer I place the machine in to the tub. Even though the machine has little feet it stands on, I would suggest placing the machine on something so it's elevated, maybe on a dolly. The reason for this is b/c first the drain hose is a gravity drain hose, so the machine sitting higher up means it will drain water better. 2nd the drain hose is short and if machine is not elevated on something, then that water is draining in to the tub and all around the feet of the washing machine, which just happens to be plugged in to an outlet. Just safety safety...
Now, I did not elevate my machine in the tub, but I positioned the washer in the direction where the drain hose is right by that tub drain and draining in to the drain.
I am currently looking for some kind of base to set my washer on when I place it in the tub.
I have to say, I think that this is a great little washer spinner. I am very very happy with it. I actually look forward to washing clothes. The machine washes the clothes really well, the clothes come out nice and clean, they smell nice. I get to do this from the convenience of my home and the only time for a trip to the laundry mat is to wash the big comforters.
When the washer first arrived it came packaged with it sitting on a nice styrofoam base... I kept that base and when I'm done washing I place my washer back on to that base. It's very neat clean and tidy.

The top shelf in the configuration the fridge arrived in will hold 25 upright cans (not 15). All the other shelves you have to lay the cans down and get 15. And the bottom bucked holds 15.

If you lay the cans down on the roomiest shelf, stack more on top, you can get 27 cans.

At this point. 82 cans. Still missing those 8.

I’ve included photos. If you can figure it out, kudos to you.

Realistically though, if you want access to the stuff you put in here. 70 cans is your max.

title: Good Fit, Easy Replace. Does it Filter, Why The Bad Taste?
text_original:
Early on I used only genuine GE MWF replacements due to the superior NSF rating for filtering harmful substances. All were consistently good.

Later, I spent a fair amount or time researching various cheaper replacement GE MWF filters and their NSF/ANSI claims (Or lack of). I tried several and though I never had bad experiences, I came to realize they were NSF 42 filtering only chlorine and very minimal solids.

Then I found the Waterdrop Plus which offered filtering claims similar to OEM GE filters… at a much better price. I saw lots of 5 Star reviews and quickly purchased a 3-pack which arrived the same day.

I immediately went about replacing the old filter, currently a GlacierFresh brand, with one of the WDP-MWF which I pre-filled with cold water. I noticed the slightly different vent slits in the design of the filter seal but the cartridge twist-locked into place just fine. Next I ran about 1 1/2 gallons through the filter to purge any loose carbon particles. Then came the big taste test moment:

For the first time ever after replacing a filter, the water tasted quite noticeably BAD, like I was drinking from a rubber hose. So I ran another 2 gallons to purge more. Still tasted bad.

This caused me to go back to take a look at ALL the Amazon reviews I overlooked where I found several 1-Star reviewers who experienced bad taste. Even worse, those who had performed water tests showing poor filtering results of these filters.

So how about all those great 5-Star reviews? I scoured them and could not find ONE that backed up their opinion of how well the filter worked using a water test result.

If my water’s taste improves I will update my review. In the meantime without more water tests to prove filtering effectiveness, I remain somewhat skeptical given the bad resulting tests reported.

title: Good product, bad directions.
text_original:
The directions are not clear, but the cleaning elements worked great.

The kit contains two of some of the smaller pieces that are necessary and easily lost.

The handle is not for winding and unwinding the flexible cable as some reviews suggest. The handle rotates the cable to assist with snaking the cable past blockages.

My dryer has a 16 foot section between two 90 degree bends that hadn't been cleaned in thirty years. I manually fed the cable from the outside and couldn't get past all the build up. After cleaning and reattaching the inside venting to the dryer, I started the dryer and ran it while using the small 2" brush from the outside. Large pieces of lint came loose. I filled a plastic grocery bag with all the debris. When I finished, no more lint was sticking to the cleaning head, the cable banged metal on metal as I fished it in and out, and tumbling of the clothes in the dryer was heard through the now clean vent pipe outside.

A clear parts list and better directions are needed before this is a five star product. The plastic housing and crank seem sturdy enough for home use, but only time will tell.

title: Nasty Oder and HIGH surface temperatures
text_original:
I too had the problem with this GE range (but the Black model) and like you GE was as useless as they were for you. I had to run the Self-Clean procedure 4 times at 5 hrs each time in order for the smell to go away even when trying to cook something in the oven at 350 degrees.

Be aware that when doing the Self-Clean, the top of the oven (where the burners are), the metal of the electronic controls (where the knobs are and the keypad), and the front of the oven will get to over 180 degrees. The sides of the electronic control panel during the Self-Clean cycle will get to over 220 degrees.

Also when cooking something in the oven at 450 degrees the metal of the control panel with the knobs and electronics get to over 125 degrees and the side of the control panel gets to over 155 degrees.

I asked GE if this was expected or normal and they brushed me off and said that is how they designed it.

I do not know if all hidden-element, glass-top ranges are like this but GE would rather not have customers know this.

title: Door sensor keeps failing: HOW TO FIX IT
text_original: I purchased this from another online appliance place back in late 2014.  After maybe 3 years something I had in the fridge went bad and rotted/oozed while I was on vacation.  I think its that Kambutcha junk my wife drinks.  No big deal - cleaned it up but after that the fridge was never the same.  The summer after that water would always pool at the bottom of the fridge and spill over.  I thought I had wine that was not corked shut but it turned out to be that the evaporation system was not working right ans water was pooling instead of being evaporated properly.  In the back is a small drain that was plugged up with some nasty sludge - it seems that my wife's Kambucha had evolved to something more nasty than what comes in the overpriced jug from Whole Foods!  I needed to clear the sludge plugging up the drain but to clear it completely you really need to disassemble the entire back of the fridge!  After disassembling the back (about 16-20 screws) I used an air compressor and pipe cleaners to clean all that nasty stuff out and the water could freely drain properly - my water/evap issues were solved.  Soon after my fridge would continuously alarm that the door was open and the light would come on (as if the door was open).  There was no mechanical switch to be seen so I assumed the switch must be magnetic.  As it turns out it was.  Apparently the water from my previous problem had pooled inside that folded metal seam at the bottom, rusted, and swollen that folded metal so that magnet sensor in the lower left of the fridge front could no longer sense the magnetic gasket on the door when shut.  For about a year I could wipe this all down with soapy water and it was often enough to make a better seal and trigger the sensor but eventually the rust became too much.  In the end I had to take the bottom plastic trim off and it you look top the left (if you face the fridge) on the bottom is a thin pair of wires that go to the sensor.  They un-clip easily.  If you take the longer end that runs into the computer circuit and just short out those two wires it tells the system that hte dfoor is shut.  An old school PC jumper worked perfectly to short these 2 pins for me.  The door is always shut now as far as the fridge is aware so no alarm ever.  However there is no automatic light when the door opens. but you can choose to have the light on all the time (3 small LED lights do not use much power) or leave it off all the time - or manually turn it on and off as needed with the bottom on top.  Its annoying but a lot better than contestant door open alarm beeping.  I'm annoyed that a $2K small fridge was designed in a way that this could happen.  If they just sealed that bottom lip where the sensor lived water would not have been able to get in and start to rust, however I knowledge that it started with a spill that I was responsible for (darn that Kambucha).  What did I learn?  It doesn't pay to buy higher quality appliances because all are for the most part poorly designed and there is no value in paying for an appliance brand name.  When this breaks I plan to toss it in the trash and buy the cheapest replacement I can find at Sam's or Costco, assuming it will fail in 5 years or so anyway.

title: Don't use these gadgets, Use "My-Kaps" with used K-Cups
text_original:
I have purchased and used, ekobrew Cups, EZ-Cups, and Solofill cups. None work as well as the original K-Cups. Everyone of these produces weak coffee in comparison to the original K-Cups. If you like strong or flavorful coffee stay away from these gadgets. Since these versions of K-Cups use a metal screen filter instead of paper filters they let water run through too quickly so very little of the the flavor is steeped from the grounds. The EZ-Cup does not have a metal filter but it does not hold enough grounds so it also produces fairly weak coffee also. I grind my coffee in a Baratza Virtuoso burr grinder at a 15 setting. If you must use one of these K-Cup contraptions, buy the ekobrew and used the paper filters that are made for the EZ-Pod, that combo produces the most flavorful and strongest coffee. The ekobrew holds the most volume of coffee, and when combined with the paper filters the coffee steeps longer as the cup of coffee is produced.

So, after all my disappointment with these things, I now reuse my original K-Cups and use "My-Kaps" on them (get "My-Kaps" on AMAZON). There are several manufactured K-Cups that hold a greater volume of coffee. They all have a small plastic spacer that sits under the filter at the bottom of the K-cup. You can tell that it has one if you shake the K-cup before brewing. If it rattles it has the spacer, keep it after you brew it, peel the foil off, dump the coffee, rinse it with hot water, then let it sit out to dry. Barista Prima Columbia, Newman's Own Oraganics Extra Bold Special Blend, and Tully's Kona Blend all use this type of large capacity cup. I am sure there are others that I don't know about.

I use two different setups. If I grind coffee ahead of time I use Glad Press and Seal on the K-cup. I push it down into the K-Cup with the My-Kap. Then I put them in the K-Cup Carousel for use later. This keeps air away from the coffee and it stays fresh longer. There is a video on Youtube covering this process. Just make sure that you poke a hole in the middle of the press and seal after you put the My-Kap on it and before you put it in the brewer. If you don't sometimes the machine won't pierce it automatically and you will have a leaking mess to deal with as it tries to brew.

My second method, which I prefer is to grind coffee fresh, put it in the K-cup, place the My-Cap on it and brew it immediately in the Keurig Machine. I do make one modification however. I leave an outer ring of foil attached to the K-Cup so I can fold it in over the inner lip of the K-Cup. The ring of foil is created by only cutting a small circle of foil out of the middle. This foil around the edge makes the My-Kap fit tighter and results in a better seal against the My-Kap so virtually no water leaks around the My-Kap when brewing. Sorry, no video anywhere on this one. This is my tweak.

You can reuse the original K-Cups over and over. I don't know how long they will last because I have yet to wear any out and I have been brewing K-Cups this way for at least 9 months.

title: Decent washer, Terrible Customer Service.
text_original:
I needed to get a small washer for my apartment because the laundromat myself and my partner go to has not been getting cleaned during the pandemic and its a serious health risk. Little did I know that buying this washer would be a thorn in my side for an entire month.
As far as the washer goes, it isn’t actually that bad. When mine finally arrived, it looked a bit beat up and there was residue inside that makes me wonder if it had been used before. I’m not too bothered by that though, I just made sure to run it with some washer cleaner and hot water before I actually put clothing in it. I think this washer would be great for a single person that doesn’t want to/is not able to go to the laundromat, or as a dedicated washer for baby clothes. It can do a few shirts and lightweight bottoms and undergarments just fine, but heavier things it really struggles with. I could only do two pairs of jeans in it at a time which was a little annoying since I only had 3 pairs to wash.
Pros: It’s small and lightweight, easy to stash in a closet and lift into the tub or shower so it can drain out. It doesn’t require a lot of water to run, and it does the job quickly. Longest cycle is 15 minutes and the spin dryer goes for 5. The spin dryer is amazing, it does a great job getting things wrung out so when you take them out, they’re almost 90% dry.
Cons: The capacity is small, and the motor smells so bad. If you do a few loads in a row it puts out a hot plastic stink, so if you separate colors and fabric types you’d have to take breaks in between loads. It also does not have a lint collector that I can see, so you’ll need to get some separately of you don’t want balls of lint all over your clothes. The cord is also pretty short, I have a really little bathroom so my outlet is pretty close to my shower but it wouldn’t reach in most bathrooms. It also drains a little on its own while it runs so I’m not sure keeping the drain tube up during the cycle is an option. It shakes a lot so I would not feel okay with it sitting on a counter. I also am not sure how long this thing is going to last, I’ll try to update in a few months how it’s performing.
The last two are a bit minor if you are abled but the knobs can be hard to turn, especially when switching over to drain the tub. It doesn’t make a huge difference for me personally but if you have difficulties with your hands it might be really challenging. In the same vein the top part of the spin dryer can be hard to take out and can require a fair bit of dexterity to remove.
All in all, I wouldn’t necessarily NOT recommend this washer if you think it would suit your needs, but I absolutely would not recommend purchasing it from this seller.
I ordered this a month prior to receiving it, which wouldn’t be a huge deal considering the current situation worldwide if the seller had just been transparent and honest from the start. It was supposed to be to me by the 20th of July, and I didn’t get it until August 5th. Had I known that I just wouldn’t have ordered this at all because I needed to get it as soon as I could. The seller falsely said it had shipped shortly after I placed the order and didn’t provide tracking which should have been a red flag, but I didn’t worry about it. Once it was six days past the day the washer was supposed to be at my home, I contacted the seller, and then two days later filed a claim for a refund. By then I had given up all hope of actually getting the item so I bought another washer from a different seller.
That in and of itself isn’t what really bothered me, it was inconvenient but it happens, what bothered me was their awful customer service. I ended up exchanging several emails with them and it was an absolute nightmare. Their team repeatedly lied to me stating that the item had either already been delivered to me or that it was on its way when the tracking number (that I finally got five days after it was supposed to be at my house) showed that it hadn’t even shipped out yet. In addition to the lying about where the item was and repeatedly telling me that I wasn’t eligible for a refund, they never acknowledged it when I told them I could see that the item had not moved at all. Never in my life has a company lied to me over and over again and I honestly am still in shock that this was how they chose to handle the situation.
I’m a really chill customer usually, so if they had just explained whatever issue it was they were having that is causing their orders to have a massive delay I would have been totally okay with it, but instead they just lied to me over and over for apparently no reason considering my refund was granted immediately upon me submitting my claim.
It got way worse after I posted a comment on their seller page stating what had happened. They went from lying to me but doing it politely, to giving me a baffling amount of attitude and trying to make me feel guilty for giving honest feedback. I work customer service myself and I have never even considered speaking like that to the worst of my customers, let alone one that had a legitimate reason to be upset. Their attitude just got progressively worse and worse as it went on, and it was just so exhausting to deal with that it absolutely is not worth getting to keep the product in the end. (especially considering that was conditional on me removing my initial feedback)
I’ll give them props for saying I didn’t have to send the washer back, but I’m not a huge fan of everything else. It would have been so much easier and more pleasant for everyone involved if they had just been honest and straightforward in the first place. Overall I’d say skip this seller and find something from someone else. There are better washers out there for a minor price difference.

title: Better than the Keurig model
text_original:
This unit was bought to replace the Keurig model that made coffee flavored water after extensive research. I am by no means a coffee aficionado, or even really a coffee lover, I just like to have a nice cup of coffee most mornings and am too frugal and selective to want to always buy a ton of wasteful K-Cups and limit myself only to the selections available in K-Cup form.

The packaging on this was very attractive with the unit suspended in a plastic tube floating in the middle of another plastic tube. The refillable cup inside was basic but functional: everything it needed to be, nothing it didn't.

After filling the cup with freshly ground store bought coffee (old burr crank grinder) it dropped right into the Keurig with no changes from the traditional K-Cup brew mode. Unlike the Keurig brand one I didn't have to remove any inserts before putting the reusable cup in. This is handy especially if you change back and forth between K-Cups and the reusable filter a lot.

The brew itself is significantly stronger than the Keurig model and is now more like coffee than flavored water. It still however is not as strong as even my basic 12 cup brewer on Normal mode. Little tweaks like making sure I had enough grounds in the filter helped get me close enough that I get by and won't bother returning it but people that are picky about their brews likely will not be satisfied. But to be honest this is designed for a quick single cup with disposable pods and minimal hassle and it really isn't fair to judge it side by side against a standard drip maker.

To clean up when done simply knock the old grounds out into the garbage can and rinse away any that stick to the inside.

Pros:
-Significantly Better than Keurig model
-Makes a decent cup of coffee
-Use your own variety/flavor
-Easy to clean

Cons:
-Doesn't work as well as nor as strong as packaged k-Cups
-Not as strong as traditional Drip Coffee Maker

title: Using for 5 years
text_original:
I have been buying these filters for my Jenn-Air refrigerator since 2014. I have had no leakages or difficulties installing them. I am fussy when it comes to the flavor of my drinking water. The tap water in my area has a slight flavor that this filter removes. They have a VOC (Volatile Organic Chemicals) rating of 200 gallons and a CTO (chlorine, taste, and odor) rating of 2500 gallons. The OEM Everydrop brand that Whirlpool family of brands recommends has a VOC rating of 300 gallons.

All these filters work by using activated carbon to absorb carbon-based compounds (organic molecules) and a few other chemicals, including chlorine. It will not remove sodium or nitrate compounds. The carbon needs to be food grade to filter water (which means the stuff that goes in the barbecue will not work; the better ones are made from coconut shells), ground to the right size, and packed well with a few other filtration materials. As consumers we can only rely on inspections of the production facilities to know what quality of carbon and components we are buying.

text_original:
Overall, I'm satisfied with this washer. Remember that an extension hose and a filter is a MUST for this product! I highly recommend getting a stand for it as well, makes it a lot easier to use.

PROS
*washes out stains extremely well, even better than traditional washers.
*no assemply required.
*the spin cycle dries things almost completely, even though it is room temp.

CONS
*Temperamental spinner! If I don't put my wet clothes in a SPECIFIC position with a SPECIFIC amount the whole washer will start raddling back and forth and sound like a rocket ship, ready for liftoff.
*Can only do like 5 pieces of clothing in the washer and only 3 pieces in the dryer at a time. DO NOT LET YOUR LAUNDRY PILE UP! You'll be stuck doing it for DAYS.
*Short spin cycles. The longest you can set it to spin is 5 MINUTES. This is extremely short if you have something thick and need to get most of the moister out. I have a routine where I tell Alexa to set a timer every 4 minutes so I can restart the timer to make it spin longer. I wish that side would go up to 15 minutes like the washer side does.

title: Serves its intended purpose well
text_original: I've had my stove for many years and used the original box as a carrier and such.  The box was so taped up with strapping and duck tape that it was almost sinful to pull it out for our tailgating events.  The stove does phenomenal things for us and we cook, fry, grill and more, so it gets pretty scuddy.  I bought the bag more to protect my SUV but it has proved to be a very adequate carrying resource.  I agree that it is a little over-sized and wish they'd provided some internal support to fill out the cavity.  Since I have to remove the legs on my stove for packing, the remaining stub legs want to poke into the fabric.  I just set it up in the cargo area on it's back (narrow)side, handles up and it slides right in on top of a collapsed table.  If you are a tailgater, this is far better than a BBQ because the accessory grills and griddles make it completely flexible as a cooking station.  I see the bag as a necessity...and a good one, to keep any cooking residue off the rest of your gear and the inside of your vehicle.  I find the price reasonable for this custom product of good quality.

title: Maybe I'm being unfair with this low rating but I think something is amiss in fulfillment of this item....
text_original:
When I received this item, I was a bit puzzled as it had 4 holes and a sticker on the bottom that said "HIC China". Some research shows that what I received was actually the HIC Porcelain Filter Cone which is available through Amazon for $2 or $3 less than this item. What I received looks well make and I feel it will do a good enough job but looking at other recent reviews of the Cilio Cone, I think others are also receiving the wrong item as they are describing a cup made in China with 4 holes instead of 1 hole. Maybe they just haven't figured out yet they were sent the wrong item. I feel bad about the one star rating but I think it important to grab perspective buyer's attention that they may not get what they are ordering. The HIC brand may well be fine but order it on it's page and save $2 or $3.

EDIT to add: The box this holder was packed in was marked with the brand Cillo but the sticker on the holder itself said "HIC".

The original grille had the two top mounting screws going into threaded plastic where the new one had metal u-clip nuts.  Improvement but with a problem.  Explained below.  The second difference is along the bottom of the new grille there where four plastic tabs that the original looked like should have been there but were snipped off.  These four tabs fit into four mounting slots on the Microwave.  The idea is you align the tabs with the MW slots slightly to the left and when fully inserted push the grille to the right locking the grille in place.  Seems a better grille fit solution but in doing the slide right part the screw nut u-clips became miss-aligned.  Now the screws only go in to non threaded holes.  I chose to leave it like this as the grille seemed attached solid and the opening and closing function worked perfectly.  I could have sheared off the four tabs and installed the new grille similar to the original but the tabs certainly made a difference in the overall fit of the unit.

title: Not a good substitute for the Braun UGSF4
text_original: I bought the Medelco #4 cone permanent coffee filter as a substitute for a Braun UGSF4 filter.  Unfortunately, it's not a really good substitute.  Although the Medelco coffee filter will fit in a Braun coffee maker, it's not as tall and tapered as the Braun UGSF4.  As a result, it doesn't concentrate the coffee as much when it is moving through the filter so you have to substantially increase the amount of ground coffee that you are using for the same strength of coffee.  So while the Medelco is initially cheaper than the corresponding Braun filter, one would end up spending much more money in the long run because you would use more ground coffee.  My advice is to search the net (including e-bay) to find a genuine Braun gold filter...even though it will likely be more expensive than the Medelco filter, you'll be much happier in the long run.

text_original: I ordered this product 1 year and 3 weeks ago, and now I need a new ice machine.  In reviewing products currently sold by Amazon, I now notice that several machines appear to be just about exactly the same design, so I started reading reviews.  It turns out that one company makes this crap and then a variety of stupid companies place their logos on the machines.  Junk is junk regardless of the brand name and I have no desire to use any of these folks for any products again.  It worked adequately enough for the year I've had it, albeit a little noisy so I gave it 2 stars .  Now it still makes plenty of noise and all the moving parts seem to be functioning fine, it just doesn't make any ice.  You spend this kind of money, it lasts JUST through the warranty and then dies?  That is a company that belongs out of business.  And these companies putting their name on a mediocre product just smacks of being a deliberate ripoff.  Planned obsolescence sux.  In looking at OTHER machines and reading independent reviews, it appears there's a superior machine that does pretty much what this one did, but it's twice the price.  So should I order a new machine every year or suck it up and spend a bucketload of money?  I don't really feel like spending $10 - $15 a month on frozen water. Even Netflix is cheaper than that, and it entertains me.

title: First One Did Not Work At All
text_original:
I am all for ordering non-OEM replacement parts and saving money where I can. I was happy to see that this was offered as a replacement part for my Samsung fridge. The filter included instructions, and everything seemed simple enough. I mean, how hard can it be to replace a filter? I had done it a half-dozen times before in older fridges.

I had this unit in and out no less than a dozen times before I finally threw in the towel. I don't know why it was impossible to get water to flow through this thing, but the fridge would just not dispense any water when it was in. I hopped on Amazon and read other reviewers with the same issue.

I returned it through Amazon and decided to try my luck with a replacement. I got the new part within a couple of days. It looked identical to the first, but when I put in the replacement, it worked the first time. I don't know if my first filter came from a bad batch or something, but there are definitely some poorly manufactured filters floating around out there in Amazon's inventory.

Now that the filter is in and actually working, I would give it 4 stars, but due to the fact that I had to get a replacement part for a defective unit, I knocked it down to three. Thank goodness for Amazon's simple return policy/process.

title: Premier range fits the bill nicely
text_original:
Originally, I had a 36" Frigidaire range in my house, and the prospects for replacing it weren't pretty. The options are the very low quality standard Premier ranges ($600) or the $3000-$5000 commercial models.

Thankfully, Premier has a 'pro' line of stainless steel ranges to fill the void. I paid $1050 (and picked it up), though you could buy it cheaper here at Amazon, but pay for shipping.

This range is not a commercial range, though it does have 'the look'. When you open the oven door, you'll notice that it doesn't have the heft of it's more expensive brothers. However, that said, if you're looking to replace an older model, and have to fill that 36" hole in your countertop, be sure to check this range out.

I got my range, and installed it in about an hour and a half. The change from natural gas to LP took about 20 minutes. The 6 burners each go from 'simmer' to 12,000 BTU. The included griddle is fantastic - it fits over the two center burners (after removing the grates) and gives excellent even heating.

I recently cooked thankgiving dinner in the oven, and could fit an 18 lb turkey, two 3 quart baking dishes AND a cookie sheet full of dinner rolls inside the oven - try that with your 30" range!

The small cabinet next to the oven is useful for storing the griddle and a couple of cookie sheets.

A few minor nits - the backsplash looks a bit outdated in it's design, and the clock/timer combo is very basic. The lack of a self cleaning oven stings a little, and, of course, the bottom broiler, while it works very well, is back breaking to use.

I love the continuous grate surface of the stove, and the powerful burners - this unit is a great replacement for my old 36" range.

To be honest, I was very leery of purchasing a range whose manufacturer I was not familiar with, but after 3 trips to the store, and countless searches online, I bought it. We are very happy with the range, and have gotten compliments on it as well.

A couple of the burners don't stay on immediately, but they still work after a few seconds of holding the knob down and I am hoping they start working correctly after a little use, like some other reviews mention, not a deal breaker regardless.  I added a picture of the regulator, because I want to make sure people know to install it, it is required and this same one is for natural gas and propane.  I also replaced the gas line with a new one, even though the old one looked perfect, because the new ones have an extra safety valve inline.  Unluckily, my existing cooktop hole was the correct length and width, but the corners were not perfect, so I had to do some granite cutting and grinding.  If this happens to you, then I suggest making a plastic room around it for you to work on, cover everything with plastic besides a couple of inches around the hole and if there are openings underneath to the drawers and cabinets, then remove everything unless you want to clean it when you are done.  The granite dust still got through to my cabinets on the bottom left and I had to clean everything in there, but just imagine if I hadn't gone to the extreme lengths I did?  Also, if you are going to buy a diamond cutting disc for your angle grinder, then look for a 3 pack at your local big name store, you are only going to need the ribbed one, but for some reason the 3 pack of 3 different blades was cheaper than a single blade, same brand, same blades!?!?  I will probably update this in the future, but I tend to forget....good luck with your cooktop searching and let me know if you have any questions.

title: Good Fridge, Terrible Freezer
text_original:
We looked at a LOT of refrigerators before settling on this model. This one appeared to have decent construction quality and efficient use of space. The bulky drawer sides in many other refrigerators encroach too much on the internal space, as do "easy-access" compartments and ice makers that are built into the doors. We wanted a fridge that didn't have any of that tom-foolery.

We really like the refrigerator compartment. The capacity is not huge, but the french doors make it easy to see all your food and have it within reach. The interior is also really well lit, which is awesome compared to our old fridge with its too meager bulbs. Our old side by side fridge was also too narrow and deep. It is questionable to me how well the passive carbon filter works, but the built in timer will remind you when to replace it. The easy to access water filter in the fridge compartment is easy to replace.

The freezer compartment is where this fridge takes a nose-dive. We have constant problems with the door not sealing properly because of the way it is constructed. We have had our ice cream nearly melt and frost to build up because of this. There are plastic gears on the door rails that supposedly keep the left and right end of the freezer door in alignment, but it is easy to nudge the door, causing the gear to skip a tooth on one side. Overfilling the bottom compartment can cause the upper wire shelf to pop out of its rail frame, which can also affect alignment. We have to frequently check the door seal, and correct the door when the gear is out of alignment. I am not sure who designed this closing system, but it need to go back to the drawing board.

The ice maker is also very poorly executed. The ice frequently gets jammed and causes the ice maker from producing anything. I pour some warm water to clear the ice (as is mentioned in the manual), and the ice maker WILL work for a few days, but jam up again thereafter. Our ice maker seems to fill the tray too much with water, so the ice is sometimes too thick for the maker to break and dump into the tray. An engineer needs to design them an ice maker that requires no maintenance. Does not seem too hard.

In conclusion: fridge compartment = A, freezer compartment = D. Overall: C+

title: Door reversal instructions and cooling performance
text_original:
Door reversal instructions are *not* included with the fridge, but I have created instructions at the bottom of this review.

Power consumed (watts): 50-75 when cooling

Beware: the manual states that it “was NOT designed to store perishable foods. Store only bottled or canned beverages.” However, since my intention is to use this as a milk fridge for an espresso machine (and because I could find no reasonably-priced similar alternative), I wanted to verify its performance. Here are the test results...

Cools to 31-38F at max (with different temperatures throughout the fridge interior); cooling begins at 45-46F.
When ambient air is 85F (as a stress test):
* Cools at ~0.8F per minute
* Compressor is 120-130F
* Sides are 96-99F
* Glass front is 66-69F

Reversing the door: The product information page indicates that the door hinge is reversible; however, the manual includes no instructions for reversing the door. Being able to reverse the door hinge is also critical for my use case. I have found that the door may be reversed by following these instructions (which are not included with the fridge, but which I determined by examining the fridge I received):
1) lift back edge of hinge cover on top, and slide towards the front.
2) unscrew the hinge from the door bottom, then top, then remove the door
3) unscrew the hinges from the body
4) remove the screw caps from the non-hinge side and move them to holes where the hinges were removed
5) screw the hinges onto the body on the desired side
6) screw the hinge to the door top, then the door bottom
7) slide the hinge cover on the top of the hinge, pulling up on the back edge while pushing the center of the cover down so that it slides securely into place.

I never submit reviews but after my experience with this machine and LG as a company, felt compelled to save other people the trouble and recommend they do not buy one.  Their customer service is some of the worst I've ever experienced.  In order to have the machine fixed for $350 through them, I have to get serviced by one of their providers they are contracted with.  They have scheduled, missed appointments and my washer has been broken for a week now with no one to come until 3 days from now (if they actually show this time).  LG has given me the run around, transferred me so many times and no one helps.  We now have a 6 month old baby in addition to our 2 year old and have not been able to do laundry for a week.  I can not even explain the frustration.  I hope if my review even deters one person from buying an LG that I have done a good deed.  Best of luck shopping!

title: When it works it's truly amazing 6 stars
text_original:
I am not sure how to fairly review this product. When it works it's truly amazing 6 stars. When it breaks, however 0 stars. I prefer to review fairly rather than emotionally. Here are the facts. I had a pot of potatoes on PB (Power Boost) to bring to a quick boil and had intended to move the control to 2 or 3 once it started. The handle of the pan was in an unsafe position and I moved (rotated it 90 degrees. There was a very loud bang, the 220 ckt breaker popped and when I put the ckt breaker back on there was an er20 alarm and an ear piercing noise from the alarm system. That was Dec 14. After the tech came to the house on 3 separate times, waiting for parts in between, he was unable to repair the range. He was being guided by Frigidaire support. After the 3rd time support wanted to replace parts that had already been replaced. On Jan 29 2015 a Frigidaire Manager ok'd a replacement which will take around 2 - 3 weeks for the new range to arrive. I had this for a month before the disaster.

My advice to anyone is NOT to move any pot or pan (Yes these were induction range approved) on PB (Power Boost). ABSOLUTELY get an extended warrantee. Realize now there is a parts availability shortage, which I suspect will eventually not be a problem.

In all fairness Frigidaire did what any manufacturer would and try to fix the range. However, 2 weeks between parts delivery is not reasonable. I don't suspect Frigidaire was the culprit on this though, but I am not sure. Don't be dumb like I was, get the extended warrantee. I NEVER get these because generally they are a rip off.

In conclusion it's a great product until it breaks. PLEASE do not move any pot or pan when in PB and I thing you'll be ok. Will I be dissatisfied with the same range as a replacement ... not at all. I was allowed to purchase an extended warrantee on the replacement.

title: Not compatible with Instapod
text_original:
I've had several models of Keurigs over the years, and with each I have used the same reusable K-cup that I bought in a grocery store with the first one. When I went to use it in the Instapod, however, it did not fit. The lid just wasn't going to close. Old trusty was going to have to be replaced. Since the problem with Old Trusty seemed to be some bulk around the top of the K-cup, I looked for something slimmer. This version seemed to fit the bill, and it even says that it's compatible with Instapod, at the bottom of the model list in the picture of compatible models.
I bet you can see where this is going, especially since I laid it out in the title of this review. No, it did not fit. The hinged didn't sit in the machine correctly, and popped up on the one side, preventing the lid from closing without undo force. The bottom only has one indent, so that was the only position the K-cup would sit in. The lid also seemed like it wouldn't have lasted long under extended use, but I'll never know.

title: It is Good, but not perfect, and I can overlook that for the price, and the size.
text_original:
(Had to update this review.) after using it for a couple months, I still love it, but it does not clean perfectly. Very difficult to get many dishes into it, and you can not cover other dishes, so big bowls can only be washed alone. Stuck on food will not come off, basically.. you have to clean the dishes by hand to scrape food off, then this machine will further clean them. The door for soap has gotten stuck a few times and did not release soap. The jets are weak, it just sprays the water around gently, but in this size washer, you can not find anything better. The more I use it, the smaller it gets, but it beats having to wash stuff by hand all the time.

I was surprised how quiet this is, but honestly I was expecting to hear some strong jets going splish splash like in the full size units. This one is very calm, quiet, and seems to be more about soaking the food off with gradual spraying of water, I can't see inside so I can't say how strong the jets really are. All I know is that all the dishes came out spotless, except 3. It seemed the pan on top with stuck food was very clean, but the bits of food landed on a lower plate that was on it's side the right way, but some how the drying stuck the food on the plate. There was also soap residue on 2 more plastic tupperware tops, so some plastic is not as easy to clean, but any glass, or ceramic, or silverware, dog bowls came out PERFECT. VERY VERY PLEASED WITH THIS UNIT!!! So Far... I just wish the jets were stronger, if there was a small dishwasher with stronger jets I'd pay more, but there seems to be none, they are all made the same in this size as far as I know.
(Update) I decided to be realistic, after eating, all dishes are dropped in the sink into water.. then they can wait all day, or 2 days until enough to put into the dishwasher, then you know all your dishes will be cleaned spotless. The normal setting seems to clean the best as it's longer than all of them. I also use Cascade pods for the best result and smell, but for a shorter wash I'd use half the amount. Tried wallmart brand and it was ok.

title: Great Monitor & Device Controller
text_original:

title: No repairman works on SPT appliances.
text_original:
NO ONE repairs SPT appliances. I bought an SPT (Sunpentown) built-in dishwasher, model no. SD-9252SS. In less than 2 years, the control panel stopped working. I called repairmen within 10 miles of here, and none of them had even heard of it. None would touch it, because they did not know the brand, did not have parts, and could not warrant the work. When I called SPT, they offered to teach me *over the phone* how to repair dishwashers, and to sell me parts from California. I am a landlord, not an appliance repairman. I asked, "What happens if the repair doesn't work? Or when it breaks again?" And the weedy little guy in California said, "Well, we can troubleshoot it for you, and recommend parts ... ."
Buy from an established brand that has approved repairmen and a parts inventory. I am now buy a new dishwasher, even though this one is less than 2 years old.

title: cooking when the lights go out
text_original:
I can't seem to get a simple answer to a simple question about this Bosch 4-burner 30" gas cooktop, model NGM5055UC. The question is: Can this cooktop be used during a power outage, by lighting the burners with a match? I am thinking of switching from an electric cooktop to gas, and the only reason for doing this is if the cooktop can be used when the power goes out (which it does pretty often around here, sometimes for days). The problem is that I've gotten lots of answers, and they're all over the map. The owner's manual that goes with Bosch cooktops (8 different models) says: "During a power failure, only the cooktop burners can be lit manually." That "only" puzzled me, since this manual applies specifically to
cooktops, not to stoves with ovens (ovens definitely cannot be used during a power outage). So I asked my question on Amazon. The first reply was "This unit has an electronic ignition, so in order to use the unit during a power failure you would need to manually light the burner." "Manually" presumably means using a match, rather than one's hands (by rubbing real hard on the burner?), but it didn't sound like the party who replied had ever actually tried it, so I asked again on Amazon. The second time I was told "unfortunately there is a safety feature built into this cooktop that is an automatic shut off and a match will not work to light the unit when power is out." What's weird about these contradictory replies is that both were signed "Goedekers" (evidently a dealer). So I continued my research by asking my question in a chat on the Lowe's website. The reply was "Yes, it can be used during a power failure. No problem." I even phoned the manufacturer -- you would think they would know, wouldn't you? The first time I phoned, I spoke to someone who didn't know the answer. She said "Just a minute, I'll have to ask," and then I was disconnected. The second time I spoke to Chuck, who told me no, it wouldn't work during a power outage, but it turned out he was basing his reply on a single phone call he had from a dissatisfied customer. I asked if I could speak to someone who knew more about the way this particular cooktop was constructed, and he took my number and said someone would get back to me, but they never did. So I am baffled. I was planning to buy this cooktop, but I don't want it if it won't work during a power outage. Isn't there someone out there who actually owns this 4-burner 30" Bosch gas cooktop, model NGM5055UC, and who has actually used it, or tried unsuccessfully to use it, during a power outage?

title: Improved replacement over the original gasket
text_original:
Great replacement for the moldy original gasket in our washer. This one has a design that seems less likely to trap water and gunk in its folds.

It is a very fussy/difficult fit, and the one I got did not come with the two white and black jobbers shown in the photo. I ended up using chapstick tubes (noted in another review) to hold the spring in place during the final reassembly (watch a YouTube video or two for the process and that will make sense). Also, use a little (not too much!) dish washing liquid to lube the gasket when stretching it over the metal flanges on the washer.

You may want to replace your drain pump (much simpler job) while you have the beast open. Think of it as preventative maintenance.

And, lastly, strong hands. You will need strong hands. And a good 3 hours start to finish.
