title: A little Love-Hate WIth the Igloo
text_original:
So - incredibly handy to have an extra source of ice. And when it's working correctly it's great, but there are a couple of issues you should know about.. I'm sure the same with most of the countertop icemakers out there since the mechanisms look to be exactly the same on many of them . And it was inexpensive (on sale for $100-ish?). But there are few annoyances.

1) There is a TINY screen filter in the bottom of the water tank, and you had better keep it clean. It's about 3/8" in diameter and therefore clogs up very easily. When that happens all hell breaks loose - water can't get to the nozzles in the correct volume. The filter is hard to get out, and very easy to lose. It would be nice if they gave you a couple extras. The first time I cleaned it it wound up down in my disposer. I rescued with no harm done, but it could have just as easily wound up in the sewer.

2) We have hard water, and even a tiny bit of calcium build up can make the mechanism start sticking, where it won't dump the ice into the bin and just shuts off.... error lights flashing. The "fix" is to run a 50-50 solution of white vinegar/water through the thing every week or two. This is a pain, and it takes a lot of flushing and wasted ice cubes, but it does dissolve the calcium and keeps it working.

3) This one is a design flaw IMO. The ice bin "fills up" when it's only about 1/2 full. As soon as one cube lands between the bin and the mechanism, it triggers the "bin full" light and it shuts off. So every time I walk by it I open the lid and push the cubes over into the bin. Much better ice volume, but another pain.

title: GE model CFSP5RKBBSS not making icecubes
text_original: My refrigerator is a model CFSP5RKBBSS. The ice cubes stopped forming and dumping. I had tried replacing the Icemaker (WR30X28693), the water valves (WR57X33326) and the Fan Duct (WR60X10330) but these were not the root cause of the problem. Instead it was a bad Ice Box thermistor, which is not shown as a serviceable part in the GE diagram (it is foamed directly into the door of the fridge) which then once failed caused the control board (WR55X11098) to fail, the output voltage to the Fan Duct was only 2VDC, should have been closer to 14VDC, causing the temperature in the cube door to be above 32F. I replaced the thermistor by cutting off the wires feeding the wiring harness and splicing in a new thermistor (WR55X10025), then replaced the control board and all is well.

title: Great igniter for low price - replaced 316489400 igniter in 790.79379405 Kenmore Elite Gas Range
text_original: We have a Kenmore Elite Gas Range model number 790.79379405 and our oven bake igniter part number 316489400 failed. This replacement was easy to install and is working great. Our oven ignites in 17 seconds now. We had been smelling a light gas smell when our oven started for a few years and had a Sears repair guy come look at it but he said it was because we had aluminum foil in the bottom of the oven. Well removing the foil didn't fix it and the igniter eventually failed. Low and behold while troubleshooting a failed igniter some articles said you can smell has when your oven starts up because it doesn't ignite and burn as efficiently. Anyway, I had to cut off the bottom tab with a hack saw and I filed it smooth, vacuumed it clean and made sure not to touch the element itself. I also broke a head off a screw taking the old igniter off so I removed the burner and was able to get the old screw out. I bought stainless screws to fix it. My gas safety valve says it is 3.3/3.6 amp and this igniter says 3.4-3.6 amp so I thought it should be fine and it is. It's working great. Great product for the price.

title: Makes MOLD as effectively as ice
text_original:
[[VIDEOID:266dab26568ee043666b097bd2c2b90d]] I have had this model for a year now and had to replace the original 6 months in. I was fastidious about cleaning the machine per GE's instructions every Monday morning. In began to notice black crap accumulating in the reservoir and didn't realize it was mold. I had been cleaning it weekly so why should I, right? The mold got worse and worse until it blocked the flow to the pump and the pump failed. I got a replacement (although it took 3 month do so). I thought maybe I was not rinsing it enough and that he black stuff was some sort of lining that was deteriorating, so I cleaned it as I did the original but rinsed it even more. Also let the vinegar and bleach solutions sit in it for longer in cleaning. Last week I saw all the black stuff again and I searched it on the internet and found out it was MOLD! My machine was just out of warranty so I opened it up and was shocked at what I saw. See photos. The tubes, interior reservoir and all innerworkings were covered with mold. I removed all tubes and cleaned the machine with a very strong bleach solution and even let it sit all night. Rinsed many times and reassembled. I operated it for one week and checked yesterday. Guess what I found in the lower reservoir again? Mold. See the last photo.

My wife and daughters have been having odd health issues that we have been trying to get to the bottom of. My wife's last visit to the doctor was when the doctor said they will be checking for mold exposure next visit. When we checked the records of when her health issues started, we found they coincided with the purchase of our Opal. Internet research shows that GE knows about this and moved the location of the inner reservoir in the second generation unit so it would not sit directly above the heat producing compressor. No recall has ever been issued. I just checked. Even though this is out of warranty as of last month, I want all my $600 back and or I am going to a lawyer and pursuing legal action against the company. I will post this on Amazon as well since that is where I got the machine. GE, you know what I want. Feel free to reach out.

title: These Do Not Work - Use Only Genuine Sub Zero Part
text_original: Please don't waste your time and money on these after market Sub Zero door gaskets. My son and I, who are both very handy, spent hours and even days trying to make this work, only to realize that after market gaskets do not contain enough magnetic force as contained in genuine Sub Zero gaskets. title: all of these ceramic oven igniters are defective
text_original:
first, I didn't get mine from Amazon or the seller but I want to write a review to help others, to encourage manufacturers to come up with a better design, and to beg sellers/shippers to PLEASE package these things better.

these lighters are defective from the beginning, they all burn out due to their EXTREMELY fragile construction. vibration, shock - and I suspect just usage - create tiny cracks that burn out. touching during installation leaves residue that causes them to burn out. I suspect heat from using the oven burns them out, as well as cooler temperatures from not using the oven. the newer ones are even thinner and more fragile than early models. bottom line is they suck. they are a poor design from the beginning. I would rather light a stove with a match or go back to pilot lights. I don't understand the physics/safety involved that would prevent using the same type of spark igniters as the stove top burners, but if those would work why not use them???!!!

finally, these need to be handled and packaged with EXTREME care. shoving them in a box with a couple pieces of foam and dropping them in a loose bubble envelope to be tossed around by delivery people isn't sufficient. in my case, my range was still under a full service warranty but I had to pre-order the part as the contractor didn't have any and Sears has some weird procedure where the customer orders and takes delivery of parts. when the repair was about to commence (a month later, thanks "Sears" way to use up some more of my warranty period) the new part I had ordered and left for the technician to open (because I already knew how fragile these things are) was already broken. thank DOG he actually did have another on his truck and it is working for now. I am planning to order another to have on hand as I know it will burn out soon enough - as they all seem to - and my warranty will be over. easy enough to replace IF it doesn't arrive pre-broken.

remember - do NOT touch the dark grey sparkly part and look closely for tiny cracks even if it miraculously arrives intact.

title: Sludge in the cup (and a better alternative)
text_original:
I had high hopes for this product (I even bought two from Amazon), but it proved to be unsatisfactory for me. The concept is great. However, instead of the paper filters used in drip coffeemakers, the Ekobrew Cup employs metal mesh screens in the cup to filter the brew. The holes in the mesh are tiny, but not nearly small enough to filter out the very small particles (appropriately called "fines") that are present in virtually all pre-ground commercial drip grind coffee. So what you get using all the supermarket ground coffee I tried (Yuban, Folgers and Peet's) is a cup of coffee with a layer of sludge that settles in the bottom of the cup and a slightly gritty feel on the tongue when you drink it.

Notably, the similar Solofill refillable Keurig K-cup which I purchased at a local supermarket also filters the brew through metal mesh filters in the cup and similarly allows very fine particles to pass through into the cup of coffee. There is a little less sludge in the bottom of the cup because the Solofill's mesh filter is finer than the Ekobrew Cup. But the end result is the same -- far from satisfactory. If you buy coffee beans and use an expensive top quality grinder you can probably overcome this problem using a coarser grind. However, I cannot recommend either the Ekobrew Cup or the Solofill for anyone using popular brands of store-bought ground coffee.

Fortunately, I finally located a similar refillable Keurig K-cup system that works perfectly with the three different brands of coffee I tried above. It is the "Perfect Cup EZ-Cup" (available in stores and online from Bed, Bath and Beyond). The $14.95 plastic EZ-Cup is similar to the Ekobrew, but it uses preformed paper filters ($4.99 for 50) that are inserted into the cup before adding the ground coffee. No particles or sludge and great tasting coffee -- highly recommended.

title: Please READ my review before the video
text_original:
[[VIDEOID:9f6d6752ca59982ef95afcd5dbcd06b5]] I wanted to use the ice maker a few times before reviewing it, because a 5 star review with "looks nice, haven't used it yet" is pretty worthless. Received it mid-April 2022. Waited 2 days to let coolant settle as recommended, wiped out the inside. I chose this ice maker because you can invert a water bottle on top and not have to keep filling the reservoir. I used 1-gal bottle of distilled water. Like putting a bottle on the water cooler, it takes a knack to flip the bottle and set it on the nipple w/o spilling half the water. I used a step-stool so I was see what I was aiming for on top of the machine. The ice maker calls itself "countertop" model so it fits on the counter, but its the size of 4 toasters stacked 2 on 2, so its not going to live on my countertop.
So, plugged in, first gallon set on top, (the water reservoir holds a little less than 1-gallon so there's still water in the inverted bottle. It siphons nicely), pushed buttons per instructions and she started right up. Instructions are pretty clear, the ice maker is not overly loud (well, for my house anyway) after cooling itself a minute or 2, the screen shows the number of minutes to make ice. Each cycle of ice "sheet" took 5 minutes, but I didn't time the entire gallon of water, and I didn't weigh the total ice produced. I didn't want to babysit the process, so I just did other stuff until I heard the ice drop into the bin, then transferred it to zip-bags into freezer. The included "scoop" is useless and now resides in my cat's kibble. I did see a few comments about the ice melting in the bin. It MAKES ice. It's NOT a freezer. So, yes, you have to transfer the ice to your freezer within a few minutes. I didn't pay attention to "start to finish" time but noticed it sat idling for a few minutes before checking the reservoir was empty of water. I had 4 'full' gallon-size zip bags plus one "sheet" of ice. So, I used 2 gallons of water, in 2 days of ice making, that time.
A few weeks later, early May, I brought out the machine and made ice from another 2 gallons of distilled water. It worked like a champ again! It was quiet to run, I didn't babysit the process.
4 gallon bags of ice does not keep my family going for a month. Yes, we purchased ice between time. I'm stingy and kept my ice for me.
So... now it's end of June, I have my 2 gal of distilled water and nothing going on on my countertop for a few hours, might as well make ice! I set it up, it ran smoothly, I heard the first batch of ice drop into the bin, I put it in my bag then into freezer. Ice maker starts its new cycle, a minute or 3 later.... - OK, NOW WATCH MY VIDEO - standing next to the machine, the screeching startled me enough to drop my glass of ice water! I pushed the button to pause the machine! Eyebrows up in my hairline, I decided to "look under the hood", like a motorist on the side of the road with no clue what to look for. Still full of water. I pressed the button again and it started its cycle, me with my phone ready to catch sight of the screaming demon that has possessed my ice maker! Yup, it screamed, I paused it again.
Now... my dilemma - do I let it run? Sacrifice my machine to save a buck-50's worth of water?? (Like spending $40 more to save $5 shipping) So... I decided if it's still running it can't be too bad, if the motor is burning out - might as well see if I can get a little more ice out of it.
I had my fire extinguisher handy, moved the machine as far from the elec outlet as the cord allows, so I can unplug it, and I let it run.
When the machine is paused, it shows the temperature of the water (?) which was normally 75°F to 80°F. The temp showed 92°F! But I went ahead and let it screech. Normally the cycle time is 5-6 minutes for ice. It showed 18 minutes now. 12 minutes into the scream cycle the screaming stopped, the machine continued running and continued its countdown. It finished its cycle at normal motor decibel. Then it started the cycle again, a few minutes in, it starts screeching again. Pausing showed 88°F but I let it continue and again the noise stopped after about 10 mins. I unplugged it after the ice cycle completed. As I was yelling at the machine to "SIT THERE AND THINK ABOUT YOUR BEHAVIOR!!" my husband gave me the eye roll, moved the machine around, set a little fan blowing on the machine's exhaust intake screen, told me to stop torturing my toys, and think about my own behavior. Oh, and would I make him a sandwich, please?
I turned the machine back on later in the afternoon, it screeched only a few minutes during each cycle but made ice. This morning it's running quietly and finishing a gallon of water.
It was hot yesterday - 100° outside. It was warm inside - probably about 80° - we don't have a/c in our old farmhouse. I'll use it when the weather is cooler or until it dies a loud painful death when the weather is hot and I want ice!
So, as far as recommending this ice maker, it depends on what you can tolerate.
No extended warranty is offered, but it would be nice if it did.
Edit: Oct 2022. 70°F I've been making ice for about 3 hours with nary a squeak from the ice maker. Seems the motor is highly sensitive to weather/temp and likes it cooler. Which kinda defeats its purpose for ice in the hot summer months...

title: Repeated heavy leaking from bottom of unit, even after warranty replacement.
text_original:
I really wanted to love this dishwasher, and I did initially, but after the first one leaked from the bottom within months, and now with the first warranty replacement leaking in the exact same way, I just can't recommend it to anyone.

Both times, the leaking from the bottom began after the sink didn't drain quickly enough and the exhaust hose became fully submerged. But then it continued leaking huge amounts of water from the bottom during every wash, pouring out onto the counter and floor and making a big mess for me to clean up.

When it worked, it was fantastic. Cleaned dishes well (still does), wasn't fast but was very thorough. But there must be some kind of design flaw that makes it permanently leaky when it experiences ANY water pressure within the unit, due to slow draining.

I don't know what I'm going to do now. A $200 appliance that's only a few months old, and my three options are (1) another warranty replacement, (2) get some sort of tray to put underneath and channel all the leakage to the sink, or (3) try to fix it myself, and possibly void the warranty.

I'm at my wits' end with this.

That translates into fewer dishes that can be loaded, and the need to run it more frequently. To make matters worse, the arrangement of the angled (rather than straight up and down) tines makes loading large or odd shape items more difficult. In combination, the dishwasher holds considerably less than my old one.

And the industrial designer who thought it would be cool to hide all the buttons and indicator lights should be sentenced to using this dishwasher daily for the rest of his life. There's no visible indication when the cycle is done, or where in the cycle it is. You can't stop a cycle without opening the door a bit, which increases the possibility of splashing water on the floor. The Kitchen Aid has a "clean" indicator light that stayed on until you reset it. The clean light on the Bosch goes out a few seconds after you open the door. Not a problem if you live alone, but if multiple people share the same dishes it's not always obvious whether the washer has been run or not. Just really poor design.

title: Beware - The item sold by Parts-4-Less as part number WD12X21976 is NOT the OEM part as in photo.
text_original:
Be aware that the item sold by Parts-4-Less as part number WD12X21976 is NOT the OEM part as in this listing photo. I have supplied a black and white photo with the OEM part WD12X21976 from the manual. Notice the placement of the locking tab.

I have also supplied a photo comparison of what they are shipping. They send you a base ring for you to replace the OEM base in your dishwasher so their filter will work. I guess this is fine if you want to get a screwdriver out and go to work. See the instructions they send with the replacement filter. The problem is I want to exchange out the filters, keeping both and have one always clean.

To do this with the Parts-4-Less solution requires me to buy another filter and throw away the OEM WD12X21976 part I have. The listing should be changed to show the replacement part, the new base, and the instructions on how to make it work since it is not plug-in-play as OEM part would be.

Not the solution I am looking for so this is being returned to Amazon and I'll buy elsewhere that has the original OEM part WD12X21976.
I hope this was helpful and if I would have had this information in the first place I would not have ordered.

title: Not tall enough for Bunn coffee makers
text_original:
Although Amazon suggests buying this along with a Bunn coffee maker, the Bunn coffee makers require a taller filter. The re-usable filter they sell bundled with this coffee maker on Amazon is the standard (shorter) size so you can't really use it with this coffee maker (unless you like wiping grounds out from the inside every day that splash up on the inside). So what I do is put one of the tall Bunn paper filters inside the re-usable filter (which initially was an attempt to slow down the water and brew stronger coffee). The tall paper one keeps the grounds from splashing around and I just lift it out and throw it away. The re-usable filter keeps the hi-tech water-slowing-down-device (i.e. a piece of tin foil) in place. I later send Bunn an email asking if they sold a permanent filter and here was their response:

"Unfortunately, we do not sell a permanent filter for our home machines and as far as we know, there is not a permanent filter on the market that is tall enough to accommodate the amount of water at one time that is distributed from our machines when brewing. Most of these permanent filters are too short."

title: Cool and compact but has an annoying hum
text_original:
A wine refrigerator is a useful tool to have if you plan on aging any fine wines. This unit is attractive and compact for the number of bottles that it holds. Nice features include a tinted glass front door (for keeping UV light out), easy-to-read temperature gauge reading and setting right on the front door, internal light and sturdy shelves.

As with any other inexpensive compact wine fridge (based on reading other product reviews), in some ways this one is no different. It's designed to hold 20 standard/Bordeaux-style bottles. As soon as you start getting bigger (Burgundy, Champagne, and definitely not a magnum), they probably won't fit. The tapered bottles of a Cotes du Rhone and a Barolo in my collection were tight but I was able to get them in.

My biggest complaint and my reason for removing a star is that the refrigerator has a hum/buzz when running. It's never "off" though it does ramp up even louder when first turned on or when re-cooling after the door is opened. It's not overly loud, but the frequency (centered around 750Hz) I find very annoying, to the extent that I will probably unplug the refrigerator if I'm going to spend any significant time in the room. It may just be the way thermoelectric cooling works and sounds. A friend's refrigerator (different brand) makes a similar hum but is much quieter.

I did contact Whynter support via email and they were responsive within 4 hours. While apparently the level and frequency of the hum is normal for this unit, I was happy to get a non-canned response so quickly.

title: Imperfect but doing the job
text_original:
6/1/2018 UPDATE: The thing's used up. The spin drum won't spin evenly anymore (i.e. useless) and the drainage function of the wash chamber is mostly plugged up so it takes forever to drain. Almost 3 years of use, so no major regrets.
ORIGINAL REVIEW:
I've had the thing maybe 6 months now (?) and am really appreciating it so far. I'm not a fan of the laundry room in my complex, so it's great to be able to do my washes in my own private yard. When not in use, it tucks away nicely in my mini-shed, but I can pull it out and set it up in about a minute's time. It's considerably more work and attention/brainpower to monitor your load and manually switch it from one wash cycle to the next, but the trade-off for the privacy and not having to get rolls of quarters is well worth the extra work, in my opinion.

SOME PROBLEMS:
- The instruction sheet is ridiculously useless. Almost to the point of being funny. You'll do better just figuring out how to use it yourself.
- The intake hose and the connector by which the hose is supposed to fill up the washer is a joke. The hose has no connector on either end to attach to a garden hose, kitchen faucet, or anything. It's just a plastic hose and the ends are basically like they've just been cut off with scissors. One end does slide fairly snugly into the hole on the top of the washer, but since there's nothing to hook the other end up to, the water intake system is pretty much pointless. HOWEVER: it's pretty easy to just fill the washer by feeding the end of a garden hose through the door on the top.
- The spin chamber seems like it may not last much longer. Sometimes I have to turn it on and off 2 or more times before it starts spinning (similar to a manual transmission car with a bad clutch -- you can hear the motor working but it's just not quite engaging the chamber to spin). So far, I've always been able to get it working by turning it off and on again a few times, but if that stops working, the machine will be vastly less useful and I might have to rethink my feelings about this thing. title: Don't Waste Your $$
text_original: First of all, this is a Maytag product.  They just put the Jenn-Air name on it to sell it for more money!  This cooktop is not worth the money.  I admit I prefer gas cooking, but this thing takes forever to heat up, doesn't seem to get hot enough, and doesn't have a setting to tell you if the burners are still hot after you turn them off.  I can't tell you how many items we've melted plastic because someone set something on a still warm burner.  But the REAL reason I hate this cooktop is how difficult it is to clean.  Yeah, it might be fancy with the modules, downdraft vent and grease catchers, but it is horrible to clean.  Each module has gaps around it, so the module insert itself gets grease and grime on the edges, then the insert underneath it, then the main cooktop frame and housing.  Not only that, but the incredibly bright (sarcasm there) people who designed it didn't allow for the downdraft shaft to be removed for cleaning.  And you can't get to it with your hand (unless you have your kids do it!)  You should see the undidentifiable food items down there.  I can see some arborrio rice, but the rest is just yuck.  So, if you cook a lot and like to clean even more, this cooktop's for you.  I suggest going for a better conventional cooktop (but still less than this baby)and using a George Foreman grill or your outdoor grill. But if you still think you want this one, I have one to sell you! :)

title: Wrench does not fit perfectly, but was able to make it work
text_original:
Says universal, but it does not fit the 1 and 11/16th nut that must be removed to replace the tub seal. If you need this wrench, it would be wise to read reviews on some of the other wrenches for sale to see if they fit this nut better.

I made this wrench work though but wrapping a couple of the sides several times in duct tape. This helped fill in the gaps between the wrench and the nut and also held the two part wrench together. Its also important to note that I had to hit the wrench relatively hard many times in order to get the nut to even budge. I just wanted to include in case someone else experiences the same as me.

I also wanted to note that I thought the tub seal was the issue to my leaking washing machine. The fact that I had the top load washer door closed, I didn't notice that the water was slightly overflowing the tub and causing water to come out of the bottom of the washer. It turned out to actually be a small amount of build up where the air tube connected to the tub. This kept the pressure switch from being activated. As a result, the tub continued to fill and would not agitate as usual. The simple and free fix was sucking up water into a straw and blowing out the debris clogging the small plastic piece connected to the outer tub (the location where the air tube attaches to the tub)

title: Buy the cheaper, upgraded part instead!
text_original:

title: NOT Compatible with al GE refrigerators
text_original:
Caution - This may not be compatible with your refrgerator! We've used these before and they worked fine in our GE GFE29HMEES side-by-side (with the filter horizontal in the upper left of the refrigerator compartment. Apparently, between the last "lot" (a year ago) and this lot, the manufacturer changed the connection fittings. The first filter, installed in June, leaked a little (few drops) on install, and when we moved it a week ago to install the second, there was evidence of a bit more leakage. When we installed the second (last week), it leaked a LOT, puddling on the top shelf after the "purge" and continued to leak even after we re-seated it. So, I went to Home Depot and got a "real" GE filter (at about 2x the price). I looked at the two, and the GE filter is RADICALLY different. First, it has a LABELED "front" and "back" and instructions that caution to install it "front facing out". More importantly, where the filter fits into the housing, on the GE filter, there's cam that is clearly used to "pull" the filter snug into the housing. On the replacement filter, there's no such cam.

In the attached Photo, the GE filter is on the left

title: Does a good job of raising humidity in a bedroom
text_original:
Does a good job of raising humidity in a bedroom. When the outside humidity drops below 5%, this unit can raise the humidity in a 200 sq ft room to about 33% with the door closed. That makes a big difference for sleeping comfortably with allergies. I run the unit on high, and find the fan sound from the unit helpful to sleep.
It would probably take 2 of these units running on high to achieve 50% humidity in a 200 sq ft room when it is under 10% humidity outside.

CON
The water supply base should be 3x larger to last for 24 hours between fill ups. Perhaps a larger base could be an optional extra.
I live in an ultra dry climate at 2600 foot altitude so the unit will consume a full tank of water (or even slightly over the max fill level) in about 9 hours.

title: If Keurig wanted you to use your own coffee, they would have come up with a better reusable filter
text_original:
The two stars I give this are for humility's sake... just in case someone out there can figure out how to make a good cup of coffee with this thing, then it deserves two stars. I sure can't figure it out. I even looked up tips for how to make a good cup online, and found this hack where you cut up one of the plastic, pre-filled K-cups and use it to help maintain the proper pressure inside the My K-Cup ([...] and it helped a little, but this thing is still not worth the price, or the price of the entire Keurig.

It's nearly impossible to recreate whatever magic happens with those tightly engineered, reusable, landfill-filling K-cups with this loose combination of parts and your own coffee. I experimented with various water levels and amounts of coffee to no avail. As I mentioned, finding the K-cup hack online made a marginally acceptable cup, but the whole product is really a mess, from preparation, to water squirting out in all directions as it drips through, to sediment on the bottom of your coffee cup that looks more like powdered hot-chocolate leavings than anything I've ever seen from coffee.

Using the My K-Cup hack above results in something approaching coffee, but without it your coffee will probably taste like coffee-flavored water rather than a brewed cup.

In short, don't buy the My K-Cup. And if you were thinking of buying a Keurig to only use the my K-Cup because you're a good environmental citizen, don't buy the Keurig then, because there are many better quick and compact ways to make a good cup of coffee that won't result in landfills being overrun by little plastic coffee cups.

title: Changing original review
text_original:
Great ice, terrible support.

This unit makes great ice. However, it's very prone to problems. It needs to be cleaned far more frequently than the product support documentation states. Absolutely should be used with a water filter unless your water is impeccably free from sediment or other impurities. The water pump can be loud to very loud--akin to the noise put off by a normal window air conditioner in the room. And these units can run hot--mine did so to the point where it was melting the ice in the bin almost as fast as it was making it.

Support for these devices is terrible. Typical interaction turnaround time with support takes 3-5 days, so they can email you a question or ask you to do something, and if you get back to them right away, it takes another 3-5 days for a response. Then if they agree to send a replacement (refurbished) unit to resolve the problem, they need to get one in stock, which takes several weeks. In my case, I've had a support ticket open for two months now as the replacement unit was louder and had the same overheating problem as my original unit so I sent it back. I would expect far better support for a $500+ appliance.

title: Prone to Damage
text_original:
I want to like this fridge, I really do. It is a great color, great size for our basement, and has a great retro look. But Frigidaire needs to WORK MUCH HARDER to package this item. The first fridge that was delivered had a pretty busted box on the bottom, so I wasn't surprised when I opened it to find several large dents, but some of the dents were higher up and couldn't be explained by box damage. OK, I assumed rough handling by the shippers caused the issue. Contacted Amazon, they shipped me a new one (no cost, Amazon Returns was VERY easy to work with and super helpful). Well, second fridge, no box damage, everything looked fine, opened the box and dents in the door. No way this was because of the shipper as box was pristine and I watched them unload it myself. Amazon gave me a partial refund to keep it as by that time the fridge was sold out on the website.

Again, want to love it, and I am happy with the way Amazon handled this, but I think Frigidaire needs to rethink their packaging. Buyer beware, as you have seen in this review as well as several others, you're probably going to get a dented fridge.

title: Exact match with plug. No wire splicing needed. ...
text_original: Exact match with plug.  No wire splicing needed.  Removal and install was simple.  Open oven door slightly, lift and door will lift off.  Then remove 2 screws at the front of the bottom cover plate.  Remove cover plate.  Then, remove 2 wingnuts holding burner distribution plate on.  Lift off burner distribution plate.  Remove screw next to ignitor.  Remove screw holding small protection plate over the gas tube nozzle.  Now, remove burner assembly and disconnect wire from ignitor.  Remove 2 screws holding the ignitor and replace.  Install new ignitor and install burner.  Test oven before putting burner plates and cover back on.  You may have to close door or hold down door switch to light the oven.

The basic Wash cycle is the power-on default; everything is pre-set, the perfect setting for the average to-the-top-of-basket load.  There's a lot of intelligent "under the hood" digital control going on. Spin rings out water really well.  It's fairly quite even with bathroom (my location) door open, very quite when door is closed. NEGATIVES: As everyone says, supplied hose sucks- it's only long enough if machine is right next to water supply. Crappy materials, too.  I went to hardware store, bought quality hose and facet adapter for under $30. Learning to use the drain hose can be a little tricky; I find the lower the hose can be (the less height the pump has to pump), the better.  I have my hose draining into a shower (low, no bath tub).  I suggest weighing down the hose at open end (I'm using a big seashell with rubber band), otherwise, upon draining, the hose can flail around squirting a lot of water everywhere- So, heads-up.  The drain hose is not robust, I suggest babying it.  That said, it does seem easy to replace.  Now, I'm just curious how long this machine will last before something significant needs repair.  So far, it's really quite excellent (now that I've learned it's little kinks).  Even if it fails, say, in a year or two, and is not worth fixing- a new one is under $200.00!

title: Didn't Last Very Long
text_original: I bought four of the TH-10 Sonoffs about a year ago, and of those, one is still working with no problems.  The other three stopped working at various times; typically after about three to six months each.  Each time, the "ap" on my cell phone indicated that there was no longer contact with the TH-10.  Each time, I took the non-working TH-10 in close to the modem/router, and the "ap" indicated that I was able to re-register and re-name it, but the blue light on the TH-10 itself kept blinking, indicating that it wasn't able to reconnect with my modem/router, and the "ap" on my cell phone confirmed this.  I didn't try to return any of the non-working ones.  As I recall, I had bought at least some of them direct from the manufacturer, i.e. I ordered direct from the manufacturer in China, and paid same.  But when they arrived, I noticed that the shipper was inside the U.S. and it made me wonder if the stock was in fact, "new", or was it perhaps "reconditioned" (?)  Each time a TH-10 stopped working, I considered its cost vs. the hassle of trying to return it, and the shipping cost involved, and decided to discard each of them.  I should have bought them from Amazon.  And yes, I just bought another TH-10 (this time I bought it from Amazon), and after several days, no problem.  The bottom line is that I need the devices.  Yes, everything that others have said about the difficulty with connecting the wires is true and no, the TH-10's apparently don't last very long (?)  But they serve a valid purpose when they work.

title: Just get a regular washing machine!
text_original:
I bought this from Walmart about 3 weeks ago. Here is what you need to know. It is HUGE! It is nearly the size of a normal washing machine, thus it is not "portable." It is quiet, but about the same noise level as a regular washing machine. The no spindle design causes the clothes to easily get tangled and thrown off balance which makes it loud and makes it shake. It also causes difficulty when you unload it because the clothes get tied in knots. It isn't that gentle even on the gentle setting because of the knot creation. It LEAKS. First the seal on the hose wasn't good on the back and it leaked there. I bought new hoses and tightened them down really well. That stopped the leak up top. Today it started leaking from somewhere down low. I checked the exhaust hose which is just clamped onto the machine and it was dry. So it must be leaking from one of the lead or drain hoses inside the unit.
Basically, for $50 dollars you can get a real washing machine and you can find a quick connect system to allow you to connect it to your sink. Don't mess around with this thing. I have to buy a drip pan for the floor now, and I have to pray every time I run it.

title: not for use with air gaps!
text_original: The stub for the dishwasher is 5/8", which is too small to receive a standard 7/8" air gap hose. I tried with an adapter, and the air gap overflowed due to too much back pressure. I ended up putting a slip joint branch tailpiece (item B000FH6EPI) in the horizontal line between my two kitchen sinks, and that works great. Had to cap the branch on this item. If you're NOT using an air gap (as required by national building codes) then you can hook the dishwasher up directly to this item and the back pressure shouldn't be a problem. Minus one star because the branch isn't the size you need for the kind of connection you're supposed to make. title: Test one out before buying to be sure it works for you
text_original:
I do a lot of field work away from home--months at a time. I don't often have a laundry center, so I bought this (another website) to minimize the pain of wringing water out of my laundry before hanging to dry. I'd been looking at the Ninja & the Panda units for at least a year, but they're bulky if you move a lot, so... Finally bought one (Ninja) and just did my first load of laundry. My impressions:

1) The unit is lighter than I expected, but still heavy enough to stay stable on the ground while spinning. It wobbles a bit on start-up, but stabilizes quickly. The motor is quiet enough that colleagues/neighbors won't hear it if they're not in the same quarters as you.

2) A small load (shorts, 4 T-shirts, 5 pairs of socks, pillow case, 1 bath towel) filled up about half the barrel once packed down moderately. I'd wrung out rinse water comfortably (no pain from twisting...), then put everything in the machine. In about 2-minutes, I collected a full Pyrex 1.5-quart dish of rinse water with some color still in it (soap?). From 2-minutes on, water only dripped out so I turned the machine off.

3) I've read a lot about the brake system failing due to too aggressive consumer use. I turned the lever counterclockwise very slowly (around 45-seconds to "off"). You could hear the motor slowing down gradually. I hope that extends the life of the brake system.

4) Most important for me is total drying time as I'm in the field and can't wait around for clothes to dry. I hung up my clothes as normal (rack, clothesline), pointing fans on them next to them with AC on. I'd prefer hanging things outdoors, but can't where I am. So it's AC + fans. It's been FOUR hours since I hung up my laundry and everything is still damp. :( Mind you, it's still summer where I am so I'm using only 100% linen fabrics (no heavy cotton...). But EVERYTHING--including very thin, short linen socks--is still damp. Far too damp to put away or use. I pulled the pockets of my field shorts inside out and hung them upside down. Anyplace with 2+ layers (seams, reinforced pocket borders) is quite wet still. Even my super-thin linen towel is still damp.

Conclusion: I used to be able to dry 100% linen in about 4-6 hours anyway. At the 4-hour mark after using the Ninja, I see laundry will need a similar amount of time to dry. This is especially disappointing. When winter comes and I'm away from home like now, it's going to be tough drying heavy cotton fabrics (jeans, sweatshirts, blankets...).

Caveat Emptor: Realize that while this machine will save your hands from wringing out water, laundry is still damp once spun. Surprising, considering how much water you collect from spinning. From the super-positive reviews mentioning "nearly dry" or "dry after hanging only a couple hours," I thought laundry would be nearly dry when coming out of the spinner and would dry completely within 2-3 hours hung in a dry room. Not so for me. Still have to set aside 6+ hours to dry clothes. For me, the money invested is saving my hands but not noticeably cutting down drying time.

**TIP** Pry at the corner and then half way up and the liner will pop off enough to access the lower screw. There is no need to pop the whole thing off. Leave the LOWER screw in place and do not remove it....there's a reason they apply silicone at the factory so the screw does not fall out! title: Important design flaws
text_original: The range hood is finally installed and works.  The reason for the two star drop is the manufacturer's lack of love for the installer and some unfortunate shortcuts they took.  The manual is just 8 pages but needs to be much longer since it leaves out a lot of details that leave the installer to waste time by having to guess at too many decisions.  Their drawings and poor English translation (Try Google Translate or hire a native speaker to edit) are also unfortunate.  There is a blue film around all of the stainless steel to prevent scratching which is not hard to peel off until you get to the many seams that clamp the film in with the metal.  I spent 2 hours razerblading the film off as much as I could.  Some of the film still exists and does not look good to me as the installer.  I removed the glass and the lights temporarily to at least get the film out of those areas.  The ceiling plate has no place for the power cord to go through and cramming it through the duct hole was not an option I would accept so I cut my own gap on the side of the duct opening which I also applied electrical tape to prevent the duct from chafing against the sharp sheet metal.  We have 7 and a half foot ceilings so we had to go with its shortest setting which also makes the installation more difficult since there is very little room to perform tasks inside the duct covers.  The duct covers being closed on the sides requires them to be put into place before the motor unit is installed which is very cumbersome when lifting the motor in place.  Three people were required at this step: one to old the duct covers to the ceiling, one to lift the motor unit in place and one to screw the motor unit in place.  I don't understand why they all design these island range hoods for 10+ foot ceilings when most kitchens are under 10 feet.  That all being said, it works well and looks pretty good as long as you don't notice the blue film still in the seams.

title: Wheel assembly arrived on time and in good shape [See update, 9/8/19].
text_original:
UPDATED 9/8/19: Downgraded from 4 to1 star. We've now had these wheel assemblies for about five months and the screws have become so rusted that the wheels do not turn freely anymore. I bought what were supposed to be the "upgraded" wheel assemblies with the newer stainless steel screws, but the ones we got have no business being inside a dishwasher.

While these wheels are not working out as planned, I really hold Kitchen Aid accountable for this mess. If they hadn't built such inferior machines, we wouldn't have to buy these poorly made wheel assemblies. Like so many others, I grew up with Kitchen Aid dishwashers, and the older ones lasted for decades without any problems. We've now owned two Kitchen Aid dishwashers over the past six years, and my MIL has one as a result of our recommendation (they work well when you first install them, but don't last very long at all). ALL of these dishwashers have had major problems within the first 2-3 years (some sooner than that). Companies like this should not be allowed to exist. They say that the new machines are more "environmentally friendly," but that's blatantly false. The mining of raw materials, manufacturing process, distribution, and final disposition of these machines -- with a much shorter life cycle than the old ones -- is far, far more damaging to the environment that the old machines that might have used a little more water and/or electricity. Sorry for the rant, but our "disposable" society is a pet peeve of mine.
..............................................................

It's always difficult to review a product before it's been in use for awhile, but these wheels are working so far. They do not roll as freely as the OEM wheels, but if the wheels last longer, then the trade-off is worth it. I really appreciate that somebody proactively decided to do something about the incredibly shoddy wheel assemblies made by Whirlpool (and related companies). Thank you for trying to find a solution to an inexcusable problem that appears to be deliberately created by the original manufacturer (presumably to sell lots and lots of wheel assemblies).

title: Good alternative to Nespresso Pods
text_original:
I was really excited to get this because the Nespresso pod coffees are too acidic for my stomach, but my husband drinks them, so it's never really worth it for me to make a whole pot of drip coffee just for myself. So, with this, I can use my own coffee and add a pinch of baking soda to cut the acidity, just like I do with drip preparation.

The hardest part with this is taking the original foils off the pods. I've found the easiest way is to just poke a hole or cut a slit with a knife, and then peel the foil off all around the edges. And you really only have to do a few pods, and then you can keep re-using them.

As for preparing the pod with my own coffee, I grind whole beans to an espresso grind (important), and then use three scoops with the provided scoop. Tamp it down with the back of the scoop, then peel the backing off one of the foils from this kit, stick it on the pod, then use the end of the brush (the plastic end) to press the foil down around the rim of the pod. Then push the edges of the foil down around the edges. That's it! I've only used these with the espresso sized pods, and it works well in the machine.

When you're done, it's super easy to take the foil off using the little tab. It just pulls right off. I do wish there was a better storage area for the foils, brushes, and scoop, but not a big deal. You're really just paying for the foils.

title: HORRIBLE!!!
text_original: Believe the reviews!!!  We did not and we are paying the price.  I would not buy any GE product again after this purchase.  It may look okay but the quality is ridiculously subpar.  The service from customer relations is even worse.  We have had this refrigerator for all most 11 months now, and we have had 3 service calls for a number of reasons.  First of all, the refrigerator is loud.  I didn't believe most of the reviews on this and thought how loud can it be.  Well it does sound like 100hp compressor is operating in this refrigerator.  The first issue we had was with the refrigerator icing up and causing an even louder fan noise.  The second issue was with the refrigerator and freezer not keeping temperature.  Everything was warm one day and we lost most of the food.  This supposedly got fixed.  The next issue was with this unit keep things too cold and freezing everything in the refrigerator.  The temperature on the frig read out stated 37°F but the thermometer we put in there after the last incident said that is was 29°F.  I had had enough.  I asked GE to replace this refrigerator.  They then told me that they no longer make the model we had, but they could replace it with a new model that is smaller.  I told them that we could not afford to lose space in the refrigerator and we would need the same model.  They searched a little harder and found one of our models.  They shipped this to us which took about a week.  When the refrigerator arrived at 9:15pm they brought it into the house and set in the kitchen.  We then saw that the whole rear corner of the refrigerator was smashed in by a clamp truck.  This was no cosmetic damage.  It might as well been pushed off the back of the truck with damage like that.  Now they had to return this one and...this was the last straw.  I told GE that I wanted my money back.  After many phone calls and waiting for approvals on this, keep in mind we have a refrigerator that does not keep temperature, we final got GE to agree to buy back our refrigerator.  However, GE would not reimburse us for the full price we paid for the refrigerator.  At first they told me that we would be reimbursed for the MSRP price.  They said the check would be sent to the delivery company and they would deliver the check when they picked up our defective refrigerator.  A few days later I received a message from GE stating that I need to submit receipts for this refrigerator or they will not reimburse us.  I completely understood this and wondered why it wasn't done this way from the beginning.  So I submitted my receipts for the frig which included an extended warranty.  GE then told me that they would only reimburse me for what the refrigerator cost.  They would not reimburse for any taxes, state fees, or warranties.  I had already checked with the warranty company and they told me the warranty was nontransferable so the warranty was useless if I returned the refrigerator.  We are still arguing over this issue I plan to take this as high as it has to go until GE decides to stand by their product and reimburse us for the money that we laid out for this lemon of a product.

title: Pragmatic review with free advice
text_original:
It's a nice little unit but some things to note down.
1) separate your whites
In today's day and age we're spoiled with really nice washers that keep clothing bleeding to a minimal, this is not a nice industrial washer and clothes will bleed-splatter like blood in a slaughterhouse

2) Draining is a pain.
Comes with a really short draining tube and forgetting to move the knob from "drain" on the previous load will result in disaster. My advice, just keep it in the bath tub at all times during use

3) Use small loads
You may have some nice clothing hangers to dry out your loads, but that won't speed up the laws of physics, and the more wet clothes the longer it will take. Also, I wouldn't hang them in the tub, as you might want to take a shower. Hang the clothes in a separate room and put a plastic tub under them.

4) This thing is loud. That is, living on the third floor of an apartment, having this thing run in the bath tub it will be heard. As little as my trashy neighbors mean to me, no one wants to be approached by a pissed off alleged criminal without any sleep due to your washing machine vibrating in the tub for hours on end. Again, small loads should remedy this.

Overall, is a nice unit and does what it's supposed to. The only reason for the downgrade in stars is mainly the noise and finding a convenient way to drain it. Just follow my advice and you'll be fine :)

title: misleading
text_original:
I have a Samsung dryer that likes to eat the lower back drum roller at a rate of one per year. When I found this kit with the description stating "double bearing design, more stable and quieter than ordinary single bearing" and the fact that it was cheaper than buying a set from Samsung, this seemed like a no brainer. Since the OEM rollers come with no lubrication, I add some synthetic grease to help them last longer. When I removed the shaft of the rollers I found that they are not different than the OEM single sleeve bearing. See the two pictures that I took of the rollers with the shaft removed. I also attached a screen grab of the image claiming these are double bearing rollers. Since I needed a working dryer and these seemed no worse than the OEM rollers, and cheaper, I choose to keep them.

I will say that the belt that connects the drum to the motor is actually slightly wider, and seemed to be better than the stock belt. So I did choose to use it rather than the stock belt when I put the drum back in.

title: One of the best purchases I ever made for home maintenance
text_original:
I am totally not understanding the negative comments regarding the ProDesign Window Washing kit. It is amazing. I have been using one
( YES the ORIGINAL ONE that I purchased in 1990) and I think that I can comment even though I did not purchase thru Amazon. People who have problems obviously don't know how to attach the wand that clips on to the handle properly. There is one side that has a long sharp rigid edge and this has to be to the up side or, yes, it will disconnect and you will be frustrated. If you need a picture of how to put it together correctly, just ask and I'll go take a photo.
I just came in from cleaning 14 sets of windows (some of them 5' x 5') in about 35 minutes so I don't understand anyone saying that they can't be "efficient" with it's use. Yes, you swap the two pieces out (the swab wand and the squeegee) but this takes only a matter of seconds. If you don't like the swapping, buy two.
I used this ProDesign for about 20 years without problem. When the spring broke a few years ago, I contacted the company and they promptly replaced the entire handle for free. THAT was great customer service. I also replaced the squeegee once in 27 years. The one I use now is still fully flexible and does a perfect job with no tell-tale water left on the window. I anticipate that it will be good for many years to come.
My home has windows 2 1/2 stories up and I can reach with this attached to a long pole (don't remember where the pole came from and if i bought it from this company all those years ago). Even at that stretch, the unit is strong enough to put pressure on it to squeegee the windows perfectly. The swivel of the head is invaluable to me as I have 2nd story trapezoids.
Besides cleaning the windows on my home numerous times a year, I have used at at other peoples homes to reach their 2nd story windows. It is used a LOT. I congratulate the company on it's excellent product.
I have not received any product or compensation for this review. I simply love it.

title: My Broan 36SS is very quiet, when it's turned off!
text_original:
I give the unit 5 stars for looks, but when it's turned on the racket sounds like buck-shot rattling around in a metal can. Position 1) is fairly quiet, 2) and 3) sounds like someone trying to wrinkle up plastic packing.

The installer told me that the noise is the two halves of the damper? /flapper banging around inside the 7 inch pipe. I suspect that the air flow at level 1) is only sufficient to move lightweight aluminum, a heaver material wouldn't open. The higher air flows causes the two halves to flutter / rattle in the pipe.

The range surface is 21 inches from the filter screens. I tried a smoke test with a punk stick on the right front burner.
Setting 1) the smoke stream was hardly disturbed. 2) smoke started to move towards the screens but seemed to be effected by the return air from the outer top surface slits. 3) the smoke was definitely whisping towards the filter screens. My speaking voice was the same volume as the fan. At level 4) the noise and rattling was louder than normal speech, but the smoke was being sucked out. Guess I'll have to find a decibel meter to check the actual noise level.

I did ask the salesman about a fan that had the motor in the attic, but the cost was excessive, so I bought the more economical Broan Allure.

My final thoughts;

If you don't like something change it, If you can't change it, change the way you think about it!

Would I buy this model had I known about the sound, probably not.

title: Your home will smell like your dryer; use only in dry climates; screw heads not the right shape
text_original:
I have been wanting to try one of these for a while now. While we do have a vent to the outside of the house, it has always kind of bothered me that we threw away so much heat during the winter months. This allows us to pump that warm air back inside to get a bit more use out of the heat our dryer makes. This also means that you will be pumping whatever your dryer and wet laundry smell like into your living space, so you'll need to figure out how to address that. We put a few drops of cinnamon leaf oil onto the mesh filter, and that helps quite a bit. Pick your favorite scent, and also make sure to deodorize your dryer and ducts regularly.

A WORD OF CAUTION: This directs water vapor into your home. If you live in a humid environment, you will likely end up with moisture build-up which leads to other difficult issues like mold. We live in Colorado, and our home humidity is under 40%. Our vent is also near our furnace in the basement, so the humidity is redistributed throughout the house. Make sure you plan this out.

The included screws were not designed to work with the mounting holes on the back. The holes were meant to work with flat-headed screws, but the included screws have smaller and round-ish heads. You'll need to make sure you have the right screws.

title: Durable, practical and extremely easy to use.
text_original:
I bought this item on June 1, 2018. It was delivered promptly and I immediately put it to use. I am not a coffee drinker but drink tea, daily (both hot and cold). My favorite type of tea is masala chai. I make up a half gallon at a time. I boil the tea five minutes, add the whole milk, then bring to a boil, again. Then I pour it from the pan into the half gallon wide mouth mason jar that has "the tube" inside. I use the infuser as a filter. Hardly anything gets through the tube. It is extremely well made. In addition to filtering even the fine stuff, it is EXTREMELY easy to clean. After filling the mason jar, I slip the tube out (using my rubber insulated grill gloves as the boiling water is HOT). I gently dump the "grounds" into the waste basket and simply rinse the tube under the hot water faucet. It cleans so easily (not like other infuser's I have used. I like this so much that I recently bought another one for a friend.

It also works extremely well as a direct infuser for bulk whole leaf tea for cold brewing. Yeah, I have both Masala Chai AND cold brewed British Blend for both iced tea and hot tea in the frig at all times. Hey! Who knows when a friend might drop by(:>)).

These pods are a great idea, but no matter what coffee you use, the results are just not that great.

Nespresso pods have bar codes on them so the machine knows how much pressure, water and spin time to use to generate the desired coffee, and whatever bar code is on these pods makes a weak, somewhat bitter cup of coffee.

I've used Cafe Bustello, Starbucks whole bean and other brands and just can't get a good cup from these pods. However, if you use original Nespresso pods and refill those, the results are consistent and good.

So if you're looking for a reusable pod solution, spend a little money to get some original Nespresso pods and refill those.

title: Just a temporary fix.
text_original: First make sure that you get the right part number. For my SAMSUNG RF28HMEDBSR/AA the part number is 2.0 FASTENER HINGE DA60-00314C  POM  1-6. Not available on line, so I ordered from SAMSUNG. Not in stock, and won't be shipped soon. Anyway I placed the order for 5 pieces, $1.85 a piece + $6 shipping. These plastic things cannot survive for long, so you need many of them, and replace properly. The most important thing to focus, is the left door with water/ ice option. If this door sinks down then the seal at icemaker creates a gap, and the icemaker builds in ice, stops working, and if not treated fast, ice expands and the plastic cracks, creating more problems. To adjust the door - open the drawer to see the lower hinge.Insert the hex wrench into the shaft of the lover hinge. Adjust the height turning the wrench. You can make coarse adjustment adding snap rings, but you have to make fine adjustment with the wrench. Good Luck.

title: Worked great for the price
text_original:
This kit includes a few different items. My dryer was squeaking really bad, and I am a DIY person, so I decided to buy this kit and see what I could get myself into. Unfortunately I did not take any pictures, but will try to be as detailed as possible on the parts included in the kit.
The 4 drum rollers work great, but definitely not OEM quality. The rubber portion of the drum rollers seems cheaper and more flexible than the OEM rollers, but time will tell if they hold up.
The retaining clips/triangles are of good quality and very tight.
The idler pulley has two separate sealed bearings on the inside race, instead of one bearing like the OEM idler pulley. Again time will tell if it holds up. My original idler pulley bearing was seized/wouldn’t spin freely, so I would assume that’s where my squeaking issue was coming from.
The drum belt was too short/too tight for my model Maytag dryer, but wasn’t a big deal because the original belt had no visible damage.
Overall for the money I paid, it is definitely worth it, especially to get rid of the annoying and constant squeaking noise.
There are a few parts in the kit that I did not use, assuming this is a universal kit for several different style dryer models.
From tear down to vacuuming out the dust/lint to putting everything back together, took me 1.5 hours or so.
I will update this review if the new rollers or new idler pulley give me any more issues.

Someone took their hands and put them in the box in stacks, that is obvious.
I've worked in warehouses and know what crawls around in and around cardboard boxes, even ones that are new, unassembled and I'm not so sure this one was. Plus they used their hands to pack them, warehouse gloved or not doesn't matter. So that is too unsanitary for me to put my coffee water thru and drink. There was no paperwork in the box either. The box was taped closed very amateurishly, like one of my kids did it. On top of that it has been raining and the moisture and humidity made all feel damp inside.
Not that it would have mattered as the thought of hand packing a food touching product and placing it in an unsanitary cardboard mailing box was just not something this doctor mom was willing to use.
I ended up calling Amazon b/c it looked like it couldnt' be returned. But the representative clarified that it can be refunded which she sympathized with the ick factor, refunded me the big $12 and was passing the packaging info on.
The filters may work great but I'm not so sure I want to try that again if this is how they ship out.

title: Mediocre
text_original:
I waited until I had used this dishwasher for a full year in order to give a fair assessment. I will start with the positives. The dishwasher was well-packed. It arrived much faster than was originally promised, and it did not arrive damaged (unlike a previous dishwasher I ordered online). Another positive: the dishwasher looks nice in my kitchen, and I like the full stainless steel tub. I think the dishes dry better because the steel tub retains heat better than a plastic tub.

Now for the negatives. If you want clean dishes from this dishwasher, you will need to do two things: pre-rinse your dishes well and always set the cycle to “heavy soil.” If you are looking for a dishwasher that gets off dried on food and heavy food residue, look elsewhere. As for noise, it isn’t terribly loud, but it HAS gotten louder over the course of the year that I have used it, and that is concerning. The dishwasher does not feel well-built, and I do not expect to get many years of service out of it. Already, the wheels on the lower rack have worn out and won’t turn properly, making it hard to roll the rack in and out. As others have noted, the rinse aid dispenser has never worked right. It displays an empty code within a couple days of refilling it whether I put a lot in or a little. It never worked right, and I have given up n trying to use it. It just wastes expensive rinse aid. The design of the upper dish rack seems fine for fitting dishes in, but the lower rack has so many unmovable tines so close together that it is very hard to get many of my dishes to fit right. I handwash a lot of dishes that I used to put in th3 dishwasher because there is simply no way to fit them into this dishwasher. A word of advice, don’t try to put anything tall next to the door when loading the lower rack. The detergent will not dispense properly and the dishes will not get clean. Also, the dishwasher cleans better with powdered detergent. I tried a couple different gels and the dishes had a film on them (even with rinse aid) until I switched to powder.

All in all, though, you’d be better off with a dishwasher that is more solidly built and cleans more reliably.

It stopped by removing the filter but it took some time to soak it all back up- VERY annoying. We didn't have this problem at all when installing the original Samsung brand filter. We were finally able to get this installed correctly by putting it in quickly and locking it in. Be warned, if it's making noise and you can hear the water flowing, it's in wrong and will flood your fridge.

title: Danby beverage cooler
text_original: Unit arrived undamaged and worked right out of the box. Door was assembled a bit crooked and overall quality is mediocre but looks good from a distance. Have had it about 5 weeks now and it is doing its job- drinks stay sufficiently cold, good capacity, internal fan helps a lot (main reason I bought it) and is quiet enough in my family room adjacent to my home theater setup. Stopped working once for some unknown reason (maybe got a bit hot as I have it installed in a tight cabinet space- IFU clearly says it is designed to be free-standing) but after unplugging and letting it sit for 30 mins, it started up again and has been fine ever since. I check the external cabinet temp regularly and while it does get quite warm to the touch, it seems to be okay installed as is. A good idea is to keep it out first time it cools down your drinks (it will work quite hard doing this), then when the compressor cycles off (ie- it has reached its set temp), you can push it back in. Overall it seems to be a good deal for the price.

title: First one failed. I'm on my second unit, will update!

It was just as easy to install as it was to take off the original part. I installed it and it worked great. About 1.5 weeks later my dryer kept tripping the breaker. I checked the wiring everything was good. After taking the element off I noticed burnt carbon on the housing. I'm guessing it shorted out. There was some deformation of the heating coils as well that indicates the coils .as not have been made of high quality metal <--just a possibility. Long story short I returned it with no problems and reordered this same element hoping it was just a fluke. I received the replacement very quickly and when I proceeded to install it I realized I mailed my thermostat with it **face palm**. I ordered a replacement thermostat kit and it came quickly. After some rewiring I was able to install this replacement and it all works! I'll give updates on how well this second element works and if it fails or not! Thanks for reading!

text_original:

I have a small, detached greenhouse that I was using it in and after awhile, the humidity reading was always at 99%- which it definitely was not at, according to the other gauges I had inside. Also, the display would fade out to the point of unreadability. So I stopped using it and got something else. Then I decided to put it back in this winter to just use it for the thermostat function, as my other thermostat doesn't have a day/night differential option. It worked for maybe a month, but early this morning I woke up to my low temp alarm going off. Seems the plug where you plug the heater in decided it didn't want to work anymore.
If this item was humidity resistant and had better quality parts, it would be perfect. I realize that under normal use (reptiles, terrarium), where most of the unit is outside the monitored area, it probably would've lasted longer. However, I've seen other people using it in their greenhouses and have no problems. Bummed that it didn't work for mine...

title: Nice Compact Dryer.
text_original:
First off, this is a very nice, easy-to-use, compact dryer. This dryer fits in my apartment and saves me from making trips to the laundromat (and spending more money in the long-run). I wasn't sure how to vent it at first... at first, I just put a sock over the exhaust duct (to catch any stray lint/dust) and let it vent to the room. This worked temporarily while figuring out better options, but, as expected, resulted in a lot of moisture and smell (not bad... just laundry) in the room. I tried indoor vent options, but they were either large, expensive, ridiculous, or all of the above, so I returned them. I ended up making my own window vent unit from parts from Home Depot... for about $10. Works perfectly.

The only negative point I have for this dryer (which is why I didn't give it a perfect 5 star rating) is that I do not like the filter in the lint trap. The lint trap itself is easy to remove... the lint comes off of the lint screen very easily (like any other dryer); BUT, there's an additional filter behind the lint screen. Lint sticks to that filter and is hard to remove. Usually, I end up leaving a bunch of little rolled up lint balls on the filter, because they're just so stuck to it. They sell the filters separately in packs... which makes me wonder if they get damaged trying to clean them, or just get so caked with lint that eventually they cannot be cleaned at all. I don't know, but they suck and I'm not going to buy a pack of them. I'll figure something else out first.

title: Don't do it
text_original:
We had such high hopes for this machine. It's one of the only units that does the pelletized ice which we love. However, this machine has been nothing but problems. Let's go into those, shall we?

1) The accessory tank leaked from day 1. Fill the tank up, place it on the stand, which is plumbed into the main unit, and water pours out of the bottom (see picture). Good thing I didn't walk away after loading it up.
2) The water empty indicator (it's supposed to light up the ring blue) never worked. The first we had that the machine was empty was a VERY loud grinding noise from the compressor/pump area. Had to unplug the machine and plug it back in to reset it.
3) 1 week into ownership and it has stopped making ice altogether. The vent on the right side of the machine is generally warm when the unit is running. I came to the machine one morning and it was running, but all the ice had melted and the vents were cool. Refrigeration system had stopped working.
4) This thing is noisy. Very much so. It's essentially a small compressor sitting on your countertop.
5) It requires constant cleaning (weekly), and the drain hoses in the back are very short. If it's not sitting right by your sink, then you're dragging this 50lb machine close to one, or you are using a bucket to catch the effluent.
I contacted GE Support and their answer to all of this was "send it back". really? Turns out there is a separate Opal support line. Those guys were prompt to answer the calls and emails, but generally required a lot of convincing that the unit was not working as expected and was actually leaking.

I had enough with the (many) issues with the machine and decided to send it back as a return. I was hoping for much more, being backed by GE, but it really seemed like a beta product.

title: EZ-Cup vs. Solofill
text_original:
I bought both the EZ-Cup and the Solofill at a local Bed Bath and Beyond, though I may continue buying EZ-Cup filters at Amazon. Both work as advertised, and I would rate both of them with 4 stars. However there are some differences that make me choose the EZ-Cup over the Solofill most of the time I make coffee:

1. Filters make cleanup for the EZ-Cup easier and quicker, though Solofill is easier to fill because you don't have to monkey to around with a paper filter.
2. To me, the EZ-Cup filtered coffee tastes slightly smoother and has less sludge than Solofill.
3. Although you have to buy the EZ-Cup filters, it still works out to a lot less than buying K-Cups.
4. Solofill does brew much faster than EZ-Cup, about twice as fast. I think this is because the finer filtration with the EZ-Cup restricts the water flow more. However, the finer filtration is probably why the EZ-Cup coffee comes out slightly better. (See #2, above.)

So, as with most things, there are trade-offs for each good point about a product. If coffee quality and cleanup is more important to you, I would go with the EZ-Cup. If you like the idea of faster brew time, less environmental impact, and lower long term cost, then go with the Solofill.

title: Fits cuisinart coffee pod water tank holder perfectly.
text_original: Just make sure you rinse filter in filtered cold water for 5 minutes to flush micro-granules out and clear out most of the air pockets inside the filter. If you average more than8-10 cups of coffee a day- probably a good idea to change out the filter every 2 months- every month if you don't filter your tap water (Pur, Zero water,etc.). title: Not worth it
text_original:
So I've tried to be objective about this item, but for me it's just an incredibly needless waste of time and money.
Well I ordered green but received pink and have been trying to use this weekly, but honestly find I can do my small items much more easily, in my sink, in far less time than using this incredibly time consuming gadget. And it's not any better at getting anything clean.
This thing is awkward and trying to find a usable space for it is ridiculous, due to the frame that doesnt fit anywhere usable. I tried putting it on my kitchen counter next to the sink, but getting water into it is a pain because there is no connection to it straight from the faucet, so I have to fill it cup by cup, which takes forever. Then cranking it at least 100 times, pouring/draining the dirty water out. Then filling it again, cup by cup with at least 24(!) cups of water, cranking again 50 times , draining water ,filling again, cranking,draining and wringing everything out to hang. Time used 45-60 minutes!!
Next I tried putting it in the bathtub. But once again it's a problem filling it because again,due to the frame, it can't get close enough to sit under the faucet. I even tried aiming the shower stream into it,which was a joke. So I ended up trying to fill it with a plastic gal milk jug with water, which I had to fill 3x, and pouring that(3×) into it. Still horrible time consuming, not to mention the backache from having to bend down to crank it 100+ times, draining, refilling from jug 3 more times with clean water, draining, wringing.
Then I saw a useful tip that said to use a pool noodle by hooking one end over a faucet and the other end in the bucket. Ok that worked better, for filling but STILL cumbersome and just way too time consuming. All this to wash 2 towels or a pair of jeans or 3 t-shirts or some underwear??? LOL
So, based on reviews, this apparantly works great for some, but not for me. I can see it maybe good for a few items in an RV or camping, but not for regular laundry.

title: They do work.  Maybe they changed the rubber formula back to the original.
text_original:
I purchased this as a stocking stuffer for Christmas 2021, and the recipient reports that it does, in fact, work as advertised.

I had purchased several of this item many years ago and they worked flawlessly back then, so I was hopeful, despite the negative Amazon reviews. I was prepared to assist the gift recipient in fixing or replacing the ends if they lacked sufficient grip, but again, I'm told they do work just fine. Perhaps the manufacturer paid attention to the bad reviews and fixed the issue.

The body of this tool is still just one solid piece of plastic, so the hinge has a limited life span. If they had used a metal spring hinge, this thing would last just about forever, hence why they did not use a spring hinge.

This tool is now WAY overpriced for a simple, small chunk of plastic and a couple of rubber caps. The ones I purchased locally years ago only cost about $1.50 a piece, and even that's overpriced, considering the relatively short lifespan of the product.

If yours doesn't work for you, there are fixes. If cleaning and scuffing the tips with 100-150 grit sandpaper doesn't do the trick, you can replace them with automotive vacuum line caps, which are available in many sizes at most auto stores and the rubber is usually quite grippy. I've even heard of people replacing the tips with pencil eraser-caps.
However, if they are now shipping units that are all identical to the one I bought for Christmas, the tips will work out of the box and you won't need to fix them.

I deducted 2 stars due to it being ridiculously overpriced, because the plastic hinge is designed to have a short life span.

As I began to put in standard size soda cans, I realized very quickly that I can only fit 10 cans per shelf on the first 4 shelves from top to bottom with 2 rows and 5 columns. The lowest shelf does not fit 5 columns but allows for 3 rows and 4 columns.

As someone that likes to maintain an organized appearance, this mini-fridge WITH A GLASS DOOR makes it appear like a 5-year-old just threw a bunch of cans in it. I know I have Powerade on the top two shelves in the photo. You cannot close the door without forcing it to shut with 3 rows and 5 columns on the shelves. It seems that they manufactured many of these with incorrect measurements and are still selling them falsely advertised.

Grand total of possible cans on the SHELVES is 55 when it should be 75.

PS: You can fit 3 rows of cans per shelf if you want to force the door shut with the cans pressing against the glass. I didn't try filling it up entirely and forcing it to shut, but I wouldn't be surprised to come home and discover the door opened as a result of the constant pressure.
