title: Great icemaker when it works properly
text_original: Over a period of time, the icemaker in my LG stops functioning normally.  On the bottom of the ice making tray, there is a heating element that fails over a period of time.  These elements are NOT replaceable and are molded into the icemaker.  The element heats the ice cubes slightly and the tray rotates a twists to dislodge the ice cubes.  If the heater fails to work, the cubes WILL NOT dislodge. At this point, the tray full of cubes goes back to home position.  Once it has returned to home position, the water to refill the tray goes down into the cube accumulator and then the fun begins.........the dispenser coil freezes up due to being surrounded by the water which was spilled from the refilling action.  If you allow the accumulator to totally fill with ice, the fun begins.  The icemaker is supposed to cease operation if the accumulator is full.........it does not perform that function.........Be advised, pay attention to the amount of ice in the accumulator.........it will help to extend the life of the icemaker for a time, but eventually, the tray warmer will stop functioning you are back to square one.  How to fix:  buy a replacement ice maker and install.  Fortunately, the rest of the refrigerator functions well..............so far.  I am on ice maker #5.  The first three were replaced via extended warranty.  I have this new ice maker at the ready.......The old one is on borrowed time..........NO MORE LG refrigerators.  Take note of how expensive these refrigerators are..........Do your homework!!!!  The good news, the icemaker is hard to change.......one screw, disconnect the wiring and reverse the procedure...........Do it yourself, fortunately.

title: Homebrew Failure
text_original:
This is the third unit I have owned, so I am pretty familiar with how to set/adjust the temp. My primary use is to maintain a steady and constant temperature in my fermenters for homebrewing. I'm using these thermostats in tandem with heat wraps. They have worked pretty well over the years and have kept me at my target temps within 1.5 degrees +/-. Unfortunately, one of the units stuck on last night. Despite being in a 50F degree (ambient temp) garage with this thermostat set at 68F degrees, I discovered that the temp of the fermenter rose to 82F degrees. It overshot the target temp by 14 degrees. Since this was only the second day in the primary, I'm going to assume this stout is going to taste like garbage. If it was 5 days after, I wouldn't be as concerned, but most of the action takes place within the first 5 days of fermentation.

I discovered the fault was from a defective probe. When I bend the wire near the plug, the thermostat goes from blank to reading numbers. The wire itself must have fatigue from use/coiling it when putting it away. Which is a bummer, I thought they would last for at least a handful of times before failing.

I would just write this off as just a defective unit, but after reading through several homebrew forums, I've discovered that these units fail quite often. I'm going to continue my research and see what other unit I can upgrade to.

title: Good ice, but built to fail.
text_original:
We purchased this Euhomy ice maker approximately 2 years ago. It produces consistent nice ice and generally meets our needs. However, this unit and you'll find many are almost identical internally are simply built to fail and hit the landfill.

What we noticed and what happened:

A few weeks ago we started noticing some odd behavior from the ice maker where the ice making reservoir that would normally dump at the end of an ice cycle was dumping mid-way through. We couldn't really identify what was happening and then it would immediately start working well again. Until it didn't. Once it failed, the reservoir would just keep rotating up and down non-stop and seemingly never call for water from the pump necessary to start the ice cycle.

Additionally, we had noticed that the production of ice had slowed over the last few months.

How it's used in our house:

This ice maker uses 100% filtered water. It run usually 1 day per week for multiple cycles on that day to get the ice we'd like for the following days. So in this case we've used the appliance less than 100 times. Water is always drained when we've completed making ice and the machine wiped down and dried.

How we proceeded once the unit failed.

First, I reached out to Euhomy customer service through Amazon. I did get a response that generically said "out of warranty, maybe replace the pump."

I had no expectations of a replacement unit as I understood the 1 year warranty, but I was hoping for some technical support, a parts list, etc. Nothing. No troubleshooting steps. No direction on where or how to obtain parts.

Given the option of throwing this in the garbage or giving it a chance I took the unit apart. I took apart the pump and it appeared to be in good working order, but I preemptively found a pump that matched and ordered it. After some further work and diagnosis I saw two identical limit switches (one pictured here) that are clearly depressed as part of the reservoir tilting action I mentioned earlier. With minimal testing and verifying via a multi-meter I found that one of these switches had in fact failed. I was able to locate 12 of these switches for about $6 on Amazon. They arrived and I removed the existing one and soldered in place the new one. While I was at it, I cleaned the condenser fins.

The result is the ice maker is working excellent and back to producing large appropriate ice.

For future iterations of this ice maker I'd love to see a more accessible pump for cleaning and potential replacement. This could literally be solved with a small panel in the sheet metal bottom of the ice maker. I'd also love to see these limit switches in a plug end type install eliminating the need for soldering for those that might not be so inclined. And lastly, it would be great to have a removable and washable filter in front of the AC fins to prevent buildup that invariably happens regardless of how clean your house is.

In the end this ice maker meets our needs and I'm thankful to have it, but I'm sorely disappointed in the customer service and the lack of self service options on parts that would otherwise be easily serviceable by the consumer. This gets such light use from us that I can't imagine how many of these devices are needlessly hitting the landfill.

title: OK for the price
text_original: At first I was a little disappointed in finding that the temperature measurement was 2 degrees high. I expected better. I went to the Acurite website and found that the accuracy specification for the device was +/- 2 degrees thru the temperature range of 32 degrees F to 80 degrees F. So the device did meet its accuracy specification. I expected too much for the price. As an electrical engineer that spent a career designing measurement instruments, I should have recalled that a temperature sensor alone with a measurement accuracy specification better than +/- 5 degrees F would cost more than I paid for this meter.. That's why more accurate meters are calibrated for accuracy and cost more because of the labor cost of calibration. You get what you pay for, and at ten dollars this device meets specifications at a modest price. Hence four stars. Good device for the money if you can accept temperature accuracy of +/- 2 degrees. I note that the manufacturer's specification for humidity accuracy is +/- 10%. Seems reasonable, if you need more accuracy, get out the pocket book.

title: Terrible for motion detection.
text_original:
This item is junk. If you're hoping to use this as a decent motion detector, don't buy this item. I bought 4 of them, and will hopefully return them all. My objective was to turn the lights on in a room when I get within 3 feet of the room, and use the lux capabilities to decide if its dark, turn the lights on.

It turns out that the motion detector doesn't detect anything until I am half way in the room already. We're not talking about a big room, no more than 15 feet from the wall to the door. I tried setting the sensitivity to maximum, and still, I am half way through the room before I am detected. Spent 2 hours messing with this, and gave up. The Samsung ones are far better with motion detection. If you need a decent motion detector, stay away from this product.

The lux capabilities are suspect too. They only update once an hour unless you manually adjust the setting on your hub to update every 7 or 15 mins. 7 mins is the minimum frequency of updating the hub.

title: It's a false economy
text_original:
So ya wanna save a couple bucks, right? Me too. So I bought this to replace my failed AJU73213301 inlet valve on my WT4870CW LG top load washer. It said it's compatible, right?

WRONG!

While it is physically compatible with all the right outputs and inputs in the correct positions, it is electrically incompatible.

Per the service manual, the solenoids should have a resistance of 24 ohms +/- 10%. Well, this and another one I bought here (not OEM) were both 15 ohms.

Maybe it's just my washer, but this does not work. It does stuff. It hums. It clicks. It does let water flow and stop. Just not as expected.

Save yourself some time and energy and get the OEM unit for your washer. And if you have a multimeter, check the resistance across all the solenoids of your failing unit. The number that occurs most is probably what you should see on the new one. Give or take an ohm or two.

title: The fridge all your friends will want to play with...
text_original:
Purchased this Samsung fridge as the final appliance to wrapup our change-over to stainless steel. For first 10 days, the refrigerator didn't seem to be keeping items cold in the refrigerator section. Freezer was working great (ice cream was rock solid) but refrigerator would not stay at temperature set on computer display. If I set the temperature for 34 degrees, the inside was anywhere from 46 to 55 degrees most days. Experimented for several days disabling energy saver and running on Power Cool, but nothing seemed to be a permanent fix.

I called Samsung was very disappointed with their response. They don't know much about this model yet. Level 2 support told me that I couldn't use a thermometer to measure the inside temperature. They told me that I could not use a mercury or digital thermometer because it would have to be calibrated for the fridge. When I asked what type of thermometer I could use, they could not give me an answer. I was told to trust the refrigerator to do it's job -Sure! They can eat the spoiled food! They told me that a few degrees was normal (which I accepted) but not 10 to 12 degrees all the time.....any, to make a long story short I decided to "reboot" my fridge.

Yup, it's a linux OS that runs the system and all the apps. I decided to pull the power plug for the first time since I installed the fridge and voila. The refrigerator started working correctly. Temperatures started reporting within 2 to 4 degrees of the set temperature on the control panel. So, if you buy this frige and have this problem, remember to reboot your fridge after a few days if the temperature doesn't hold.

As for the apps. yup, Pandor, Weatherbug, AP news, Picasa web album (SD Card or photos from any DLNA network device in your home), Epicurious and more all work via WiFi. Since my wife can no longer magnetically hang a calendar on the stainless steel, I showed her how to sync her IPhone with Google Calendar which puts all her appointments and reminders on the refrigerator screen for her to review every morning. Very cool. Also the NotePad option allows you to hand write notes and messages on the screen or with a keyboard. Very cool too. While the Apps are interesting and work quite well, I can't see myself reading the news or twitter feed on the door. The screen saver mode allows you to display all or some of the specific feeds.

Finally, there is a "Smart Grid" feature prominent on the display that nobody at Samsung Level 1 or Level 2 can tell me about. When you select the option, it gives you a warning that tells you a little about smart grid. It then displays an error message saying you don't have the SmartGrid modem. When I called Samsung support, they told me to just "go buy a modem". When I asked, what type and where do I "plug in" the modem board to the refrigerator, they came up blank for answers..... I suppose once enough people call and complain, they'll provide tech support with a better response.

Samsung support is outstanding! Call Samsung first before calling the retailer. They will send somebody onsite, no questions asked, to repair a $3000 refrigerator or a $350 microwave (which I bought a few weeks before which came with mfg cosmetic defects).

REFRIGERATOR: Oh yeah, how do I like the appliance as a "refrigerator". The refrigerator compartment is well lit with LEDs and spacious. Some of the door shelves needed getting used to when switching from my old Kenmore side-by-side as only certain bottles of certain heights will fit in specific locations. Seems more cramped on the doors. Inside shelve area, I can't seem to fill it with food or leftovers. The top right shelf (lowered one notch) is the one place tall enough to store bottled waters and some cold beer bottles. I would prefer to have them somewhere on the door, but they just don't fit.

COUNTER HEIGHT DOOR: The "counter-height" door is just silly. The sliding divider in the showroom seems like such a cool idea, but in practice, if you don't have solid block objects larger than the spacer, things are falling in between compartments as you poke around. COMPLAINT- The middle drawer does not come out far enough to easily see what's in the back section of the drawer. You can reach items, but you have to poke around and bend down.

FREEZER: Works rock solid and never had a problem. My wife and I complain that the ice cream is just too hard now. That's a good thing. Has section organizers but main section is just a big dumping place for stuff.

ICEMAKER: Works great but 1/4 the capacity of our old Kenmore and VERY NOISY when the ice drops into the bucket. Yeah...VERY noisy, otherwise you don't hear a thing from the fridge. Wife empties the ice bucket every morning with 3 "Big Gulp" type cups of ice she brings into work. My old Kenmore would half fill an Igloo Playmate. .

WATER DISPENSER: Works great and high pressure. Wife complains because the first few seconds the water is warm. This is because the water tube runs inside the door, behind the touch-screen computer. Water is cool after a few seconds. WARNING: Been about 3 week so far and the water still tastes and smells like the plastic reservoir. Looking forward to not having "that new fridge smell".

PRICE: Shop around. Purchased for $3300, then price discount a week later took off about $200. Then a competitor ran a Samsung 25% discount the next day and we saved another $600+ . Thank you Best Buy Price Match Policy.

AUGUST 2011 UPDATE: Refrigerator is performing flawlessly. Several software updates over the past few months have been pushed down and all the problems appear to be resolved...knock on wood. Counter-height door continues to be silly use of space with divider, Freezer is still a disorganized mess and we've gotten used to the "You've got Ice" plunk :-)

January 2014 UPDATE: Refrigerator going strong. No problems. Sorry to hear of those with problems. Remember, it's rare to find people taking the time to write positive reviews. Negative ones are much easier to pen.

title: how to fix the spray arm
text_original:
We've had our new dishwasher for a couple of weeks and it does a great job of cleaning the dishes (our Kenmore only "worked" if you washed the dishes ahead of time). The flat rack at the top for cutlery is actually a very nice feature.

But there are some strange features, as though the folks at Miele never actually lived with a dishwasher. For one thing, you can't tell when the thing is actually running. It's very quiet, which is nice, but it makes the absence of a little red light all the more inexplicable. Instead it beeps you when it's done, and won't shut up until you come and open the door. (Just what we all need; more bossing around).

My main reason for writing this review is that I figured out what to when the middle spray arm falls off. 1. Pull out the middle rack (just pull and lift; there are little tabs on the end that you have to lift over. 2. Put the rack on a flat surface, upside down 3. Fit the spray arm so that round end of the spay arm fits INTO the semicircular channel in the middle of the rack; at the same time, make sure the little hole at the other end of the arm fits on to the little peg thing at the end of the rack. (sorry for the lack of visuals). 4. then put the rack / spray assembly on end, so that you can tap the spray arm gently but smartly, so that it goes into the semicircular channel and stays there. 5. then put the rack / spray back; you have to angle it around the end peg stopper things, but it's not hard.

It would be nice if any of this were mentioned in the manual, but, as I say, I don't think anyone at Miele has ever actually used or owned their own machine.

This "lower" "higher" design is important because you want the water to go through the coffee grounds, not just squirt through the mesh. The inside lid design is good for sprinkling the water over the whole area of the cup. Makes a perfect cup of my favorite coffee.

title: If you buy this buy four M10x1.5mm flange nuts as well.

LG instructions are to reuse the flange nuts from the original rollers. Unfortunately they are the wrong size thread. They will bind up and the cheep axil meatal of the replacements will rip. I returned the broken set and purchased again. Kind of needed the dryer working again. When the next set came in I measured the axil thread and it is M10x1.5. If you buy this for your dryer double check the axil thread size and pitch of your original parts before reusing the original flange nuts.

The better option would be for the replacement part seller to include the correct flange nuts (and washers) in the package. Outside of that I do like the roller bearing verses the original axil and sleeve design. The second set of these are installed and working well.

text_original: My sister-in-law gifted us one of these machines about a year and a half ago. The ice it makes is absolutely fantastic, but there are so many problems. First of all, we started off by using water from our Burkey water filter. I assumed that would be sufficient, but it quickly became apparent that it was not. The water started getting black stuff in it. I had a friend with an opal, and she said she only uses distilled water - so I’ve started using that, and it’s helped, but not gotten rid of it completely. Secondly, the cleaning is a huge pain. It says to clean weekly, but it’s such a process, that I’m never able to get to that quickly. It says to run the water with cleaning solution through a few times, but I swear it takes like 10 times for it to work. Of course, this might be better resolved with more frequent cleaning, but what a pain! Thirdly, the machine produces so much heat! I’ve vacuumed out the fan several times, but it still produces so much heat - which in turn causes the ice to melt. Lastly, and definitely worst of all, my ice maker has developed a bulge behknd where the tray goes. Like the plastic has warped from the heat of the motor. It seems like a major malfunction which should be resolved by the company, but of course the warranty is only good for a year. The bulge causes the tray to pop out slightly which then causes the machine to stop producing ice. For a machine that costs so much, you’d think there’d be better customer care and warranties. This thing is a piece of crap - but it produces fantastic ice - when it works!
